spec.n: The Jubbah Lake and the Changing Pictures
spec.te: Did the rock art change as the lake dried?
spec.ta: هل تغيرت الصور الصخرية مع جفاف البحيرة؟
spec.desc: A connection between records on this map. At Jubbah, the rock art of Jabal Umm Sinman stands above the bed of a Holocene lake about 20 by 5 km; the oldest carvings of life-size people and wild animals are about 10,000 years old, and later panels show cattle herding, then horses and camels. About 200 km north-west, the Columns of Rajajil, standing stones of the sixth to fifth millennium BC, have wells dug beside them. To the south, mustatil builders of about 5300–5000 BC were cattle herders of a wetter Arabia. The idea: the sequence of pictures at Jubbah tracks the life of the lake, with wild-animal panels made while it held water, cattle panels as it shrank to pasture, and wells and camels after it was gone.
spec.sig: If true, the rock art of Ha’il could be read as a dated climate record, and the lake sediments could date the panels that have no inscriptions.
spec.ev: Dates and places: oldest Jubbah carvings c. 10,000 years ago, palaeolake 20 × 5 km at Jubbah (UNESCO 2015; Guagnin et al. 2017); mustatil cattle offerings c. 5300–5000 BC about 250 km south; Rajajil stones with fifth-millennium BC wells about 200 km north-west. Content: the panels change from wild animals (aurochs, kudu, wild ass) to domestic cattle to horses and camels, the order expected if water fell and herding then dry-land travel took over.
spec.an: In the Sahara, Kuper and Kröpelin (2006) showed from hundreds of dated sites that human occupation, cattle herding and rock art followed the rains southward as the Green Sahara dried between about 8500 and 3500 BC; the Eastern Sahara’s cattle-herder panels belong to the wet phase, and settlement left when the lakes failed.
spec.val: Core the Jubbah lake bed and date its layers (radiocarbon, OSL) to fix when it held water, shrank and dried; date the rock-art panels by their varnish, superimposition and the animals they show; compare the two timelines; check whether the Rajajil wells were dug just when the regional lakes failed.
dlist: Rival explanation 1: the pictures changed because new animals and new people arrived, not because the lake changed.
Rival explanation 2: the lake dried much earlier than the cattle panels, and herders used wells from the start.
Rival explanation 3: the carvings were made from ridges above the lake bed at any time, with no link to its water level.
refs: UNESCO World Heritage Centre. Rock Art in the Hail Region of Saudi Arabia (ref. 1472), inscribed 2015.

Guagnin, M. et al. (2017). Rock art provides new evidence on the biogeography of kudu, wild dromedary, aurochs and African wild ass in the early and middle Holocene of north-western Arabia. Journal of Biogeography 44, 2071–2081.
Thomas, H., Kennedy, M. A., Dalton, M. et al. (2021). The mustatils: cult and monumentality in Neolithic north-western Arabia. Antiquity 95(381), 605–626.
Kuper, R. & Kröpelin, S. (2006). Climate-controlled Holocene occupation in the Sahara: motor of Africa’s evolution. Science 313(5788), 803–807.
spec.se: The pictures at Jubbah go from wild animals to cattle to camels, carved above a lake that dried. Does the order of the art follow the water? Nobody has tested this yet.
spec.sa: تنتقل الصور في جبة من حيوانات برية إلى أبقار إلى جمال، منقوشة فوق بحيرة جفّت. فهل يتبع ترتيب الفن الماءَ؟ لم يختبر أحد ذلك بعد.

spot.en: Born from a lake bed and a cliff on this map. Jubbah’s oldest carvings, about 10,000 years old, show wild animals above a lake 20 by 5 km; later panels show cattle, then camels. To the south, cattle herders built mustatils around 5300–5000 BC; to the north-west, people dug wells beside the Rajajil stones in the fifth millennium BC. Water first, then herds, then wells.
spot.ar: وُلدت الفكرة من قاع بحيرة وجرف على هذه الخريطة. تُظهر أقدم نقوش جبة، وعمرها نحو 10,000 عام، حيوانات برية فوق بحيرة طولها 20 كيلومترًا وعرضها 5؛ وتُظهر اللوحات اللاحقة أبقارًا ثم جمالًا. وإلى الجنوب بنى رعاة الأبقار المستطيلات نحو 5300–5000 ق.م؛ وإلى الشمال الغربي حفر الناس آبارًا بجوار أحجار الرجاجيل في الألف الخامس ق.م. الماء أولًا، ثم القطعان، ثم الآبار.

tag.en: Wild animals, then cattle, then camels: did the carvers of Jubbah draw the lake drying?
tag.ar: حيوانات برية ثم أبقار ثم جمال: هل رسم نقّاشو جبة جفاف البحيرة؟

en: At Jubbah in Ha’il, a sandstone hill rises above a flat plain. The plain was once a lake about 20 kilometres long and 5 wide. On the hill, people carved pictures for ten thousand years: first life-size men and women with wild cattle, kudu and wild ass; later herds of domestic cattle; later still horses, camels and writing.

The map holds the neighbours of these carvers. Around 5300–5000 BC, cattle herders far to the south were offering horns in the mustatils. In the fifth millennium BC, people near the Rajajil stones to the north-west were digging wells. The order is suggestive: lake, herds, wells.
ar: في جبة بحائل يرتفع تل من الحجر الرملي فوق سهل منبسط. كان السهل يومًا بحيرة طولها نحو 20 كيلومترًا وعرضها 5. وعلى التل نقش الناس صورًا عشرة آلاف عام: أولًا رجال ونساء بحجم الحياة مع بقر بري وكودو وحمير برية؛ ثم قطعان أبقار مستأنسة؛ ثم خيل وجمال وكتابة.

وتحمل الخريطة جيران هؤلاء النقاشين. نحو 5300–5000 ق.م كان رعاة الأبقار في الجنوب البعيد يقدّمون القرون في المستطيلات. وفي الألف الخامس ق.م كان الناس قرب أحجار الرجاجيل في الشمال الغربي يحفرون الآبار. والترتيب موحٍ: بحيرة، ثم قطعان، ثم آبار.

en: The Sahara was green between about 8500 and 3500 BC. Lakes filled, and people with cattle spread across it, carving and painting their herds on the rocks. Kuper and Kröpelin gathered hundreds of dated sites and showed in 2006 that occupation followed the rains: as the lakes failed, the people and their art moved south.
The cattle panels of the Eastern Sahara belong to the wet phase. Where the lakes dried, the carving stopped. Climate, not fashion, set the calendar of the pictures.
ar: كانت الصحراء الكبرى خضراء بين نحو 8500 و3500 ق.م. امتلأت البحيرات، وانتشر فيها أناس بأبقارهم ينقشون ويرسمون قطعانهم على الصخور. جمع كوبر وكروبلين مئات المواقع المؤرخة وأثبتا عام 2006 أن الاستيطان تبع الأمطار: فحين خابت البحيرات انتقل الناس وفنهم جنوبًا.
لوحات الأبقار في الصحراء الشرقية تنتمي إلى الطور الرطب. وحيث جفّت البحيرات توقف النقش. المناخ، لا الذوق، هو الذي وضع تقويم الصور.

en: If Arabia worked the same way, the Jubbah lake bed holds the key. Its mud should record open water while wild animals were being carved, shrinking water while cattle were carved, and a dry pan before the camels. Date the mud, date the panels, and lay the two lines together.
If instead the lake was dry long before the cattle panels, the carvers were drawing animals, not climate. That answer would be worth having too.
ar: إذا عملت الجزيرة العربية بالطريقة نفسها فإن قاع بحيرة جبة يحمل المفتاح. ينبغي أن يسجل طينه ماءً مفتوحًا حين نُقشت الحيوانات البرية، وماءً يتقلص حين نُقشت الأبقار، وقاعًا جافًا قبل الجمال. أرِّخ الطين، وأرِّخ اللوحات، وضع الخطين معًا.
أما إذا كانت البحيرة جافة قبل لوحات الأبقار بزمن طويل، فقد كان النقاشون يرسمون حيوانات لا مناخًا. وهذا جواب يستحق المعرفة أيضًا.

spec.n: The Folds that Hold Oil and Lift Water
spec.na: الطيّات التي تحبس النفط وترفع الماء
spec.te: Do the oil-trapping folds also feed the oasis springs?
spec.ta: هل تغذي طيّات النفط ينابيع الواحة أيضًا؟
spec.desc: A connection between records on this map. The Dammam Dome, where well No. 7 struck oil in 1938, is a salt-cored anticline; Ghawar, 200 km east of Riyadh, follows the En Nala anticline on a basement horst, sealed by anhydrite. Al-Ahsa, farmed since the Neolithic, is watered by more than 280 artesian springs from the Neogene aquifer, and Jabal Al-Qarah beside it is cut by deep joint-controlled fissures. Tarout Island has been inhabited since about 5000 BC and Thaj, a walled city of 300 BC–AD 300, lies between them. The idea: the same folds and joints that trap oil at depth bend and crack the shallow aquifer, forcing water up as springs, so that the oldest settlements of the Arabian Gulf coast sit on the crests and flanks of these structures.
spec.sig: If true, the deep geology that made the kingdom’s oil also decided where its first farmers and traders could live, and new springs or old ones could be predicted from structural maps.
spec.ev: Structures: Dammam Dome, a salt-cored anticline (Dammam No. 7 record); Ghawar on the En Nala anticline, 280 km long, sealed by 30–100 m of anhydrite. Water: more than 280 artesian springs at Al-Ahsa from the Neogene aquifer; joint-controlled fissures in the Hofuf Formation at Jabal Al-Qarah (Hussain et al. 2006). Settlement: Al-Ahsa farmed since the Neolithic; Tarout inhabited since c. 5000 BC with Ubaid pottery of c. 4500 BC; Thaj walled city c. 300 BC–AD 300. Geography: Al-Ahsa (25.43 N, 49.62 E) lies about 40 km west of the Ghawar crest; Tarout (26.57 N, 50.06 E) about 30 km north of the Dammam Dome.
spec.an: On Bahrain, Larsen (1983) showed that the island’s famous artesian springs rise where the Dammam aquifer is bent and fractured over the Bahrain dome, and that the Dilmun settlements and burial fields of the third and second millennia BC clustered on exactly those spring lines, moving as the springs did.
spec.val: Overlay spring locations at Al-Ahsa, Qatif and Tarout on the mapped crests and faults of the Dammam Dome and En Nala anticline; measure artesian pressure and water chemistry along and off the structures; date early settlement layers at Tarout, Al-Ahsa and Thaj and compare with spring positions; look for fossil spring mounds and tufa along fold axes.
dlist: Rival explanation 1: the springs rise where the aquifer simply reaches the surface at low ground, with no relation to folds.
Rival explanation 2: settlements followed the coast, the sea and trade, and springs were a bonus rather than the reason.
Rival explanation 3: rainfall far inland on the Tuwaiq outcrop controls the artesian pressure, and the folds only add small local effects.
refs: Saudi Aramco. Dammam No. 7: the Prosperity Well.
Afifi, A. M. (2004). Ghawar: the anatomy of the world's largest oil field. AAPG Search and Discovery.
UNESCO World Heritage Centre. Al-Ahsa Oasis, an Evolving Cultural Landscape (ref. 1563), inscribed 2018.

Hussain, M., Al-Khalifah, F. & Khandaker, N. I. (2006). The Jabal Al Qarah caves of the Hofuf area, northeastern Saudi Arabia: a geological investigation. Journal of Cave and Karst Studies 68(1), 12–21.
Wikipedia contributors (2026). Tarout Island, citing Bibby, G. (1969) Looking for Dilmun.
Larsen, C. E. (1983). Life and Land Use on the Bahrain Islands: The Geoarchaeology of an Ancient Society. University of Chicago Press.
spec.se: The folds that hold the oil under Dammam and Ghawar may be the same folds that push 280 springs to the surface at Al-Ahsa, where people have farmed for 7,000 years. Nobody has tested this yet.
spec.sa: قد تكون الطيّات التي تحبس النفط تحت الدمام والغوار هي نفسها التي تدفع 280 ينبوعًا إلى السطح في الأحساء، حيث يزرع الناس منذ 7,000 عام. لم يختبر أحد ذلك بعد.

spot.en: Born from three records that sit close together on this map. Dammam No. 7 found oil in a salt-cored dome; Ghawar follows a long anticline; between and beside them, Al-Ahsa’s 280 artesian springs have fed farms since the Neolithic and Tarout has been lived on since 5000 BC. Oil needs a fold to trap it. Springs may need the same fold to lift them.
spot.ar: وُلدت الفكرة من ثلاثة سجلات متقاربة على هذه الخريطة. وجدت بئر الدمام رقم 7 النفط في قبة ذات نواة ملحية؛ ويتبع الغوار طيّة طويلة؛ وبينهما وبجوارهما تغذي ينابيع الأحساء الـ280 المزارع منذ العصر الحجري الحديث، وتُسكن تاروت منذ 5000 ق.م. النفط يحتاج إلى طيّة تحبسه. وقد تحتاج الينابيع إلى الطيّة نفسها لترفعها.

pred.en: Springs, fossil spring mounds and the oldest settlement layers will line up along the mapped crests and faults of the Dammam Dome and the En Nala anticline, and artesian pressure will be highest there.
pred.ar: ستصطف الينابيع وتلال الينابيع الأحفورية وأقدم طبقات الاستيطان على طول قمم وصدوع قبة الدمام وطيّة النالة المرسومة على الخرائط، وسيكون الضغط الارتوازي أعلى ما يكون هناك.

test.en: Map every spring and fossil spring mound against the structural contours; measure pressure and chemistry on and off the folds; date the earliest layers at Tarout, Al-Ahsa and Thaj and see whether they sit on spring lines.
test.ar: رسم كل ينبوع وتل ينبوع أحفوري على خطوط الكنتور البنيوية؛ وقياس الضغط والكيمياء فوق الطيّات وبعيدًا عنها؛ وتأريخ أقدم الطبقات في تاروت والأحساء وثاج لمعرفة ما إذا كانت تقع على خطوط الينابيع.

wrong.en: If springs and early settlements are spread evenly across low ground regardless of the folds, or pressure is no higher on the crests, the structural idea fails.
wrong.ar: إذا كانت الينابيع والمستوطنات المبكرة موزعة بانتظام على الأراضي المنخفضة بصرف النظر عن الطيّات، أو لم يكن الضغط أعلى على القمم، تسقط الفكرة البنيوية.

title.en: What the Oil Knows about the Springs

tag.en: The folds under Dammam and Ghawar may have decided where the first farmers of the Gulf coast could live
tag.ar: ربما قررت الطيّات تحت الدمام والغوار أين يستطيع أول مزارعي ساحل الخليج أن يعيشوا

en: In 1938 well No. 7 on the Dammam Dome struck oil at 1,440 metres. The dome is a salt-cored fold, an arch in the rock that traps oil beneath a seal. Ghawar, the largest field on Earth, follows another arch, the En Nala anticline, 280 kilometres long and sealed by anhydrite.

Beside these structures lie the oldest homes on the Saudi Gulf coast. Al-Ahsa has been farmed since the Neolithic, watered by more than 280 artesian springs. Tarout Island has been inhabited since about 5000 BC. Thaj, a walled city, sat between them. All of them needed water that rose on its own.
ar: في عام 1938 ضربت البئر رقم 7 على قبة الدمام النفط على عمق 1,440 مترًا. والقبة طيّة ذات نواة ملحية، قوس في الصخر يحبس النفط تحت غطاء. ويتبع الغوار، أكبر حقل على الأرض، قوسًا آخر هو طيّة النالة، طوله 280 كيلومترًا ومختوم بالأنهيدريت.

وبجوار هذه البنى تقع أقدم البيوت على ساحل الخليج السعودي. الأحساء مزروعة منذ العصر الحجري الحديث، تسقيها أكثر من 280 ينبوعًا ارتوازيًا. وتاروت مسكونة منذ نحو 5000 ق.م. وثاج، المدينة المسورة، جلست بينهما. وكلها احتاجت إلى ماء يرتفع من تلقاء نفسه.

h2.en: Seen before: the springs of Bahrain

en: Bahrain is a dome too. Its famous springs, fresh water bubbling up even under the sea, rise where the Dammam aquifer is bent and cracked over the island’s central arch. Curtis Larsen studied the island’s land and water in 1983 and found something striking.

The settlements and burial mounds of Dilmun, from the third and second millennia BC, clustered along the spring lines. When the springs shifted, the villages shifted with them. The deep structure of the island had drawn the map of its ancient people.
ar: البحرين قبة أيضًا. وينابيعها الشهيرة، ماء عذب يتدفق حتى تحت البحر، ترتفع حيث ينثني خزان الدمام الجوفي ويتشقق فوق القوس الأوسط للجزيرة. درس كورتيس لارسن أرض الجزيرة وماءها عام 1983 فوجد شيئًا لافتًا.
كانت مستوطنات دلمون وتلال دفنها، من الألفين الثالث والثاني ق.م، تتجمع على طول خطوط الينابيع. وحين تحركت الينابيع تحركت القرى معها. لقد رسمت البنية العميقة للجزيرة خريطة سكانها القدماء.

en: The Dammam Dome, the Bahrain dome and Ghawar’s long arch are the same kind of structure in the same rocks. If the arches lift the aquifer and crack it, as Jabal Al-Qarah’s deep joints suggest, then the springs of Al-Ahsa and Qatif should line up with the folds, and so should the first farms and towns.
Or the springs may simply rise where the ground is low, and the towns may have followed the sea. A structural map, a pressure gauge and a few dated trenches would settle it.
ar: قبة الدمام وقبة البحرين وقوس الغوار الطويل بنى من النوع نفسه في الصخور نفسها. فإذا كانت الأقواس ترفع الخزان الجوفي وتشققه، كما توحي شقوق جبل القارة العميقة، فينبغي أن تصطف ينابيع الأحساء والقطيف مع الطيّات، ومعها أولى المزارع والمدن.
أو ربما ترتفع الينابيع ببساطة حيث تنخفض الأرض، وربما تبعت المدن البحر. خريطة بنيوية ومقياس ضغط وبضعة خنادق مؤرخة كفيلة بحسم الأمر.

refs: Saudi Aramco. Dammam No. 7: the Prosperity Well.
Hussain et al. (2006). The Jabal Al Qarah caves of the Hofuf area. Journal of Cave and Karst Studies 68(1).
Larsen, C. E. (1983). Life and Land Use on the Bahrain Islands. University of Chicago Press.

spec.n: Rock Outcrops as a Map of Stone Age Camps
spec.na: المكاشف الصخرية خريطة لمخيمات العصر الحجري
spec.te: Can a geological map find lost Stone Age sites?
spec.ta: هل تستطيع خريطة جيولوجية أن تجد مواقع العصر الحجري المفقودة؟
spec.desc: A connection between records on this map. Across the Najd and the southern Nefud, every Middle Palaeolithic site in this layer sits on a particular kind of rock: Dawadmi-23 beside a dyke of fine microgranite, Jebel Abyad-1 on a hill of white quartz, Az Zu’aynah-2 next to bedrock on the edge of a braided wadi, Al Qana-1 on an alluvial fan full of rhyolite, and Jebel Umm Sanman-1 at Jubbah with its yellow quartzite. At several of them tools were made on the spot. The idea: Middle Palaeolithic toolmakers chose places where good-quality rock met water, so the geological map of dykes, quartz and rhyolite near old drainage lines should predict where undiscovered sites lie.
spec.sig: If true, geological maps of Saudi Arabia, already complete, could guide surveys straight to the most likely Stone Age sites across thousands of square kilometres.
spec.ev: Rock: DWD-23 (24.90 N, 43.54 E) lies beside a felsic dyke of fine-grained microgranite; ABY-1 (24.26 N, 44.49 E) on a white quartz hill with a summit exposure; AZA-2 (24.35 N, 44.99 E) close to bedrock exposures on floodplain margins (Groucutt et al. 2016). QAN-1 (27.77 N, 41.41 E) is dominated by rhyolite, with on-site tool production (Groucutt et al. 2016). JSM-1 (27.98 N, 40.92 E) used a distinctive yellow quartzite (Petraglia et al. 2012). Water: AZA-2 borders a wadi braidplain; QAN-1 lies on an alluvial fan; JSM-1 overlooks the Jubbah palaeolake. Distances: ABY-1 to AZA-2 about 50 km, DWD-23 to ABY-1 about 120 km. Dates: only nearby JQ-1 at Jubbah is numerically dated (211–75 thousand years).
spec.an: In Dhofar, southern Oman, Rose and colleagues (2011) recorded more than 100 surface sites with Nubian Middle Palaeolithic tools on the plateau, many of them workshops at outcrops of chert, and dated one of them, Aybut Al Auwal, to about 106,000 years ago.
spec.val: Digitise dykes, quartz veins and rhyolite from the Saudi geological maps; trace old drainage lines from satellite images; divide the Najd into equal survey cells and rank them by rock and water; survey high-ranked and low-ranked cells with teams who do not know the ranking; compare the number of Middle Palaeolithic sites found in each.
dlist: Rival explanation 1: survey bias — archaeologists looked near outcrops, so that is where they found sites.
Rival explanation 2: random foraging alone can produce links between tools and rock sources (Brantingham 2003).
Rival explanation 3: tools survive and show best where bedrock is near the surface, not where people preferred to camp.
refs: Groucutt, H.S. et al. (2016). The Middle Palaeolithic of the Nejd, Saudi Arabia. Journal of Field Archaeology 41(2), 131–147.
Petraglia, M.D. et al. (2012). Hominin dispersal into the Nefud Desert and Middle Palaeolithic settlement along the Jubbah palaeolake, northern Arabia. PLOS ONE 7(11), e49840.
Rose, J.I. et al. (2011). The Nubian Complex of Dhofar, Oman: an African Middle Stone Age industry in southern Arabia. PLOS ONE 6(11), e28239.
Brantingham, P.J. (2003). A neutral model of stone raw material procurement. American Antiquity 68(3), 487–509.
spec.se: Five Stone Age sites on this map each sit on a special rock: a dyke, a quartz hill, rhyolite, yellow quartzite. Could a geological map point to the sites nobody has found yet? Nobody has tested this yet.
spec.sa: خمسة مواقع من العصر الحجري على هذه الخريطة يقع كل منها على صخر مميز: قاطع صخري، وتل كوارتز، وريوليت، وكوارتزيت أصفر. فهل تستطيع خريطة جيولوجية أن تدلّنا على مواقع لم يجدها أحد بعد؟ لم يختبر أحد ذلك بعد.

spot.en: Born from five records on this map. Each Middle Palaeolithic site in the Najd and southern Nefud lies on good tool-making rock — microgranite, quartz, rhyolite or quartzite — and several sit beside old wadis, a fan or a lake, with tools made on the spot.
spot.ar: وُلدت الفكرة من خمسة سجلات على هذه الخريطة: كل موقع من العصر الحجري القديم الأوسط في نجد وجنوب النفود يقع على صخر جيد لصنع الأدوات — مايكروجرانيت أو كوارتز أو ريوليت أو كوارتزيت — وعدة منها بجانب أودية قديمة أو مروحة فيضية أو بحيرة، وقد صُنعت الأدوات في المكان نفسه.

pred.en: Survey cells where fine-grained rock lies within a couple of kilometres of an old wadi will hold several times more Middle Palaeolithic sites than equal cells without such rock.
pred.ar: ستحوي خلايا المسح التي يقع فيها صخر ناعم الحبيبات على بعد كيلومترين تقريبًا من وادٍ قديم مواقع من العصر الحجري القديم الأوسط أكثر بعدة مرات من خلايا مماثلة بلا هذا الصخر.

test.en: Rank survey cells from the geological map, then send teams who do not know the ranking to walk both high- and low-ranked cells and count the sites.
test.ar: ترتيب خلايا المسح من الخريطة الجيولوجية، ثم إرسال فرق لا تعرف الترتيب للمشي في الخلايا العالية والمنخفضة الترتيب وعدّ المواقع.

wrong.en: If low-ranked cells yield as many sites as high-ranked ones, the rock-and-water map has no power and the idea fails.
wrong.ar: إذا أعطت الخلايا المنخفضة الترتيب عددًا من المواقع مماثلًا للعالية، فلا قيمة لخريطة الصخر والماء وتسقط الفكرة.

title.en: The Treasure Map in the Rocks

tag.en: Stone Age toolmakers may have left a pattern that a geologist can read
tag.ar: ربما ترك صانعو أدوات العصر الحجري نمطًا يستطيع الجيولوجي قراءته

en: Near Dawadmi, a natural wall of fine microgranite cuts through the desert, and Stone Age tools lie at its foot. Fifty kilometres from a white hill of quartz covered in quartz tools, another site sits beside bedrock on the edge of an old wadi. Far to the north, people shaped rhyolite on an alluvial fan and yellow quartzite above the Jubbah lake.
These are Middle Palaeolithic sites, tens of thousands of years old. Each one sits on a rock that breaks cleanly into sharp flakes, and at several of them the tools were made right there.
ar: قرب الدوادمي يشقّ جدار طبيعي من المايكروجرانيت الناعم الصحراء، وعند قدمه أدوات من العصر الحجري. وعلى بعد خمسين كيلومترًا من تل أبيض من الكوارتز تغطيه أدوات الكوارتز، يقع موقع آخر بجانب الصخر على حافة وادٍ قديم. وبعيدًا في الشمال شكّل الناس الريوليت على مروحة فيضية، والكوارتزيت الأصفر فوق بحيرة جبة.
هذه مواقع من العصر الحجري القديم الأوسط، عمرها عشرات آلاف السنين. يقع كل منها على صخر يتكسر بنظافة إلى رقائق حادة، وفي عدة منها صُنعت الأدوات في المكان نفسه.

h2.en: Seen before: the chert workshops of Dhofar
h2.ar: حدث من قبل: ورش الصوان في ظفار

en: On the plateau of Dhofar in southern Oman, Rose and colleagues found more than 100 sites with Nubian stone tools, a Middle Palaeolithic style also known from north-east Africa. Many of them were workshops sitting on outcrops of chert, the rock the toolmakers wanted.
One of them, Aybut Al Auwal, was dated to about 106,000 years ago. Knowing where the good rock was helped explain where the sites were.
ar: على هضبة ظفار في جنوب عُمان وجد روز وزملاؤه أكثر من 100 موقع بأدوات حجرية نوبية، وهو أسلوب من العصر الحجري القديم الأوسط معروف أيضًا في شمال شرق أفريقيا. وكان كثير منها ورشًا قائمة على مكاشف الصوان، الصخر الذي أراده صانعو الأدوات.
وأُرّخ أحدها، عيبوت الأول، بنحو 106,000 عام. ومعرفة مكان الصخر الجيد ساعدت على تفسير أماكن المواقع.

en: Put the two together. Saudi Arabia already has detailed geological maps showing every dyke, quartz vein and rhyolite body. If Stone Age people chose good rock near water, those maps should work like a treasure map: survey squares with good rock beside an old wadi should hold far more sites than squares without.
It could be otherwise. Maybe archaeologists simply searched near outcrops, or maybe tools only show up where the bedrock is close to the surface. A blind survey can tell.
ar: اجمع الاثنين. لدى السعودية خرائط جيولوجية مفصلة تُظهر كل قاطع صخري وعرق كوارتز وكتلة ريوليت. فإذا اختار إنسان العصر الحجري الصخر الجيد قرب الماء، فينبغي أن تعمل هذه الخرائط كخريطة كنز: مربعات المسح ذات الصخر الجيد بجانب وادٍ قديم ينبغي أن تحوي مواقع أكثر بكثير من غيرها.
وقد يكون الأمر غير ذلك. فربما بحث علماء الآثار ببساطة قرب المكاشف، وربما لا تظهر الأدوات إلا حيث يقترب الصخر من السطح. والمسح الأعمى يستطيع أن يخبرنا.

refs: Groucutt et al. (2016). The Middle Palaeolithic of the Nejd, Saudi Arabia. Journal of Field Archaeology 41(2).
Rose et al. (2011). The Nubian Complex of Dhofar, Oman. PLOS ONE 6(11).
Brantingham (2003). A neutral model of stone raw material procurement. American Antiquity 68(3).

spec.te: Did the lava, not the builders, decide the shape of the desert kites?
spec.ta: هل حدّدت الحمم، لا البناة، شكل مصائد الصحراء؟
spec.desc: A connection between records on this map. Two lava fields 360 km apart hold desert kites, stone walls that funnelled wild animals into pens. In Harrat Kishb, more than 20 kites have shallower guiding-wall angles than those of Harrat Khaybar, and their builders worked the natural relief into the design. In Harrat Nawasif, several hundred kites cluster on the lava margins and around small wadis, mostly with two gently converging walls and simple end enclosures; one is 1.4 km long. The idea: kite design was set mainly by the terrain — where slopes and lava edges already steered animals, builders shaped the walls differently — so wall angle and length should follow the local relief more than the region or the people.
spec.sig: If true, kite plans could be read as a record of how prehistoric hunters used the landform, and the thousands of kites across Arabia could be compared on one scale instead of being sorted into separate cultures.
spec.ev: Kishb: more than 20 kites; shallower guiding-wall angles than Harrat Khaybar kites; natural topography incorporated; several building phases (UNESCO Tentative List 2023). Nawasif: several hundred kites along the lava-field margins and small wadis, on old west-to-east drainage; most with two gently converging walls and simple terminal enclosures; one about 1,400 m long with about 3,000 m of walls enclosing more than 500,000 m² (UNESCO Tentative List 2023). Al Wahbah crater lies in the same Harrat Kishb about 56 km south-south-west of the Kishb kite component. None of these kites is dated in the records.
spec.an: At Tell Kuran in north-eastern Syria, Bar-Oz, Zeder and Hole (2011) studied a huge deposit of Persian gazelle bones from the mass killing of whole herds about 5,000 years ago, and linked it to desert kites set across the routes of migrating gazelles; Crassard and colleagues (2022) later reviewed the evidence that kites worked as mega-traps.
spec.val: Map every kite in Harrat Kishb, Harrat Nawasif and Harrat Khaybar from high-resolution satellite images; measure guiding-wall angle, wall length and enclosure size; compute slope, relief and distance to lava edge and wadis around each kite from elevation data; test whether the shape measures follow terrain the same way in all three fields; date wall phases where possible.
dlist: Rival explanation 1: the differences reflect different builders, traditions or periods; Kishb has several building phases.
Rival explanation 2: the kites targeted different animals whose herds moved differently.
Rival explanation 3: walls were repaired and rebuilt, so their present angles show later changes, not the first design.
refs: Permanent Delegation of Saudi Arabia to UNESCO (2023). Prehistoric Stone Structures in Saudi Arabia. UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List, ref. 6636.
Bar-Oz, G., Zeder, M. & Hole, F. (2011). Role of mass-kill hunting strategies in the extirpation of Persian gazelle (Gazella subgutturosa) in the northern Levant. PNAS 108(18), 7345–7350.
Crassard, R. et al. (2022). The use of desert kites as hunting mega-traps: functional evidence and potential impacts on socioecological systems. Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory.
spec.se: Kites in two lava fields look different: Kishb’s walls hug the slopes, Nawasif’s are long simple funnels by the wadis. Did the land decide the shape? Nobody has tested this yet.
spec.sa: تبدو المصائد في حرّتين مختلفة: جدران كشب تحتضن المنحدرات، وجدران النواصف أقماع طويلة بسيطة عند الأودية. فهل حدّدت الأرض الشكل؟ لم يختبر أحد ذلك بعد.

spot.en: Born from two records on this map. The Kishb kites use the natural relief and have shallower wall angles than Khaybar’s; the hundreds of Nawasif kites line the lava margins and small wadis with simple converging walls. Two harrats, two shapes, two terrains.
spot.ar: وُلدت الفكرة من سجلين على هذه الخريطة: مصائد كشب تستغل التضاريس الطبيعية وزوايا جدرانها أضيق من مصائد خيبر؛ ومئات مصائد النواصف تصطف على حواف الحمم والأودية الصغيرة بجدران متقاربة بسيطة. حرّتان، وشكلان، وتضاريس مختلفة.

pred.en: Across all three lava fields, kites on steeper, more broken ground will show the same shift in wall angle and wall length, whatever field they are in.
pred.ar: في الحرّات الثلاث ستُظهر المصائد على الأرض الأشد انحدارًا والأكثر تقطعًا التغيّر نفسه في زاوية الجدران وطولها، أيًّا كانت الحرّة.

test.en: Measure every kite from satellite images and the ground around it from elevation data, then check whether shape follows terrain the same way in each field.
test.ar: قياس كل مصيدة من صور الأقمار الصناعية وقياس الأرض حولها من بيانات الارتفاع، ثم التحقق من أن الشكل يتبع التضاريس بالطريقة نفسها في كل حرّة.

wrong.en: If kites on similar ground in different fields still differ strongly, or shape shows no link to slope at all, the land is not the main designer and the idea fails.
wrong.ar: إذا بقيت المصائد على أرض متشابهة في حرّات مختلفة متباينة بشدة، أو لم يرتبط الشكل بالانحدار أبدًا، فليست الأرض هي المصمم الرئيسي وتسقط الفكرة.

tag.en: The hunters of the lava fields may have let the ground design their traps
tag.ar: ربما ترك صيادو الحرّات الأرض تصمم مصائدهم

en: From the air, the lava fields of western Saudi Arabia are drawn with giant arrows: desert kites, long stone walls that steered wild animals into a pen. In Harrat Kishb the walls bend with the slopes, and their angles are shallower than the kites of Khaybar.

Three hundred and sixty kilometres away, in Harrat Nawasif, hundreds of kites line the edges of the lava and the small wadis. Most are simple: two walls slowly closing together. One is 1.4 kilometres long and encloses half a square kilometre.
ar: من الجو تبدو حرّات غرب السعودية مرسومة بأسهم عملاقة: مصائد الصحراء، جدران حجرية طويلة كانت توجّه الحيوانات البرية إلى حظيرة. في حرة كشب تنحني الجدران مع المنحدرات، وزواياها أضيق من مصائد خيبر.
وعلى بعد ثلاثمئة وستين كيلومترًا، في حرة النواصف، تصطف مئات المصائد على حواف الحمم والأودية الصغيرة. أغلبها بسيط: جداران يقتربان ببطء. وأحدها طوله 1.4 كيلومتر ويحيط بنصف كيلومتر مربع.

h2.en: Seen before: the gazelle mass kills of Tell Kuran
h2.ar: حدث من قبل: صيد الغزلان الجماعي في تل كوران

en: At Tell Kuran in north-eastern Syria, archaeologists found a huge heap of Persian gazelle bones, the remains of whole herds killed together about 5,000 years ago. Bar-Oz, Zeder and Hole linked it to desert kites built across the gazelles’ migration paths.
The traps worked because they were placed where the animals already moved. The ground and the herds’ habits did half of the work.
ar: في تل كوران في شمال شرق سوريا وجد علماء الآثار كومة هائلة من عظام الغزال الفارسي، بقايا قطعان كاملة قُتلت معًا قبل نحو 5,000 عام. وربطها بار-عوز وزيدر وهول بمصائد صحراوية بُنيت عبر مسارات هجرة الغزلان.
نجحت المصائد لأنها وُضعت حيث كانت الحيوانات تتحرك أصلًا. فقامت الأرض وعادات القطعان بنصف العمل.

en: Put the two together. If the land did half of the work, kites on steep, broken lava should look different from kites on open, gentle ground — in the same way in every lava field. Then the different shapes of Kishb and Nawasif would be a map of terrain, not of two different peoples.
It could be otherwise. Different builders, different prey or centuries of rebuilding could explain the shapes. Measuring every kite against the ground beneath it can tell.
ar: اجمع الاثنين. إذا قامت الأرض بنصف العمل، فينبغي أن تختلف المصائد على الحمم الشديدة الانحدار عن المصائد على الأرض المفتوحة اللطيفة — بالطريقة نفسها في كل حرّة. وعندها تكون أشكال كشب والنواصف المختلفة خريطة للتضاريس لا لشعبين مختلفين.
وقد يكون الأمر غير ذلك. فقد يفسّر الأشكالَ اختلافُ البناة أو الفرائس أو قرون من إعادة البناء. وقياس كل مصيدة مقابل الأرض تحتها يستطيع أن يخبرنا.

refs: UNESCO Tentative List (2023). Prehistoric Stone Structures in Saudi Arabia, ref. 6636.
Bar-Oz, Zeder & Hole (2011). Role of mass-kill hunting strategies in the extirpation of Persian gazelle. PNAS 108(18).
Crassard et al. (2022). The use of desert kites as hunting mega-traps. Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory.

spec.te: Were the valley and plateau villages two seasons of the same herders?
spec.ta: هل كانت قرية الوادي وقرية الهضبة موسمين لرعاة واحد؟
spec.desc: A connection between records on this map. Wadi Sharma 1, about 25 km up a valley that opens to the Red Sea, is a cluster of about 60 linked stone rooms with shell ornaments, dated by 14 radiocarbon dates to the second half of the 8th millennium BC and seen as seasonally occupied. Al Uyaynah, about 106 km to the north-east on the Tabuk plateau, is a small, short-lived settlement of sheep and goat herders with more than 200 clay objects, dated to about 7190–6900 BC. The two sets of dates overlap, and the Hisma mountain corridor lies between them. The idea: these were not two separate communities but two seasonal stops of the same mobile herders, who moved between the coastal valleys and the plateau through the year.
spec.sig: If true, the earliest herding communities of north-west Arabia lived by a yearly round across very different landscapes, and their small sites should be read as parts of one system rather than as isolated villages.
spec.ev: Wadi Sharma 1 (28.10 N, 35.48 E): about 60 ground-level or semi-sunken stone structures over about 0.1 ha; chipped stone, grinding stones and shell ornaments; 14 radiocarbon dates in the second half of the 8th millennium cal BC; interpreted as a small, seasonally occupied community (Fujii et al. 2018). Al Uyaynah (28.89 N, 36.07 E): remains over about 160 × 120 m; sheep and goat husbandry; more than 200 small clay objects; main occupation about 7190–6900 cal BC; small and short-lived (Alasmari et al. 2026). Distance between them about 106 km; the Hisma stone-structure corridor lies about 44 km from Wadi Sharma 1 and 62 km from Al Uyaynah. JQ-101 at Jubbah shows Pre-Pottery Neolithic activity further east.
spec.an: In the south-western Cape of South Africa, Balasse and colleagues (2002) read the oxygen and carbon isotopes in growth bands of sheep teeth, which record where and in which season an animal grazed, to test whether prehistoric herders moved their flocks between the coast and the interior through the year.
spec.val: Sample sheep and goat teeth from Al Uyaynah, and any herd-animal teeth from Wadi Sharma 1, for sequential oxygen and carbon isotope analysis; identify the shell ornaments at both sites and trace them to the Red Sea or elsewhere; compare stone-tool and clay-object styles; look for seasonal markers in plant remains and animal ages; survey the Hisma corridor for camps of the same date.
dlist: Rival explanation 1: two separate communities living in their own areas who never met.
Rival explanation 2: one group moved once, from one place to the other, rather than every year.
Rival explanation 3: Al Uyaynah was used year-round for a short time, and seasonality there is not needed.
refs: Fujii, S. et al. (2018). Preliminary excavation report of Wadi Sharma 1, a Neolithic settlement in the Tabuk Province (2012–2013). Atlal 26.
Alasmari, K. et al. (2026). New results from the Pre-Pottery Neolithic site of Al Uyaynah, Tabuk, in north-western Saudi Arabia. Arabian Archaeology and Epigraphy 37(1), 182–206.

Balasse, M., Ambrose, S.H., Smith, A.B. & Price, T.D. (2002). The seasonal mobility model for prehistoric herders in the south-western Cape of South Africa assessed by isotopic analysis of sheep tooth enamel. Journal of Archaeological Science 29(9), 917–932.
Permanent Delegation of Saudi Arabia to UNESCO (2023). Prehistoric Stone Structures in Saudi Arabia. UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List, ref. 6636.
spec.se: A seasonal village in a Red Sea valley and a short-lived herders’ village on the Tabuk plateau were lived in during the same centuries, about 100 km apart. Were they one people’s summer and winter homes? Nobody has tested this yet.
spec.sa: قرية موسمية في وادٍ على البحر الأحمر وقرية رعاة قصيرة العمر على هضبة تبوك سُكنتا في القرون نفسها، على بعد نحو 100 كم. فهل كانتا بيتي الصيف والشتاء لشعب واحد؟ لم يختبر أحد ذلك بعد.

spot.en: Born from two records on this map. Wadi Sharma 1 was a seasonal village of the late 8th millennium BC with shell ornaments; Al Uyaynah, 106 km away, was a short-lived herders’ village of about 7190–6900 BC. Overlapping dates, one mountain corridor between them.
spot.ar: وُلدت الفكرة من سجلين على هذه الخريطة: كانت وادي شرما 1 قرية موسمية من أواخر الألف الثامن ق.م بحلي صدفية؛ وكانت العيينة، على بعد 106 كم، قرية رعاة قصيرة العمر نحو 7190–6900 ق.م. تواريخ متداخلة، وممر جبلي واحد بينهما.

pred.en: Growth bands in herd-animal teeth from Al Uyaynah will show grazing that switches between plateau and lowland conditions with the seasons, and Red Sea shells will turn up among its finds.
pred.ar: ستُظهر حلقات النمو في أسنان حيوانات القطيع من العيينة رعيًا يتبدل بين ظروف الهضبة والأراضي المنخفضة مع الفصول، وستظهر أصداف من البحر الأحمر بين لقاها.

test.en: Run sequential isotope analysis on sheep and goat teeth, identify the shells at both sites, and compare tools and clay objects between them.
test.ar: إجراء تحليل نظائر متسلسل على أسنان الأغنام والماعز، وتحديد الأصداف في الموقعين، ومقارنة الأدوات والقطع الطينية بينهما.

wrong.en: If the teeth show animals grazing in one place all year, and the two sites share no shells or styles, the two-season idea fails.
wrong.ar: إذا أظهرت الأسنان حيوانات ترعى في مكان واحد طوال العام، ولم يشترك الموقعان في أصداف أو أساليب، تسقط فكرة الموسمين.

tag.en: Two of Arabia’s earliest villages may have been one family’s two homes
tag.ar: ربما كانت قريتان من أقدم قرى الجزيرة العربية بيتين لعائلة واحدة

en: In a valley that runs down to the Red Sea, about 60 small stone rooms join together like beads on a string. This is Wadi Sharma 1. Its people wore shell ornaments, ground food on stones, and came back season after season, more than 9,000 years ago.

About 100 kilometres away, on the plateau north of Tabuk, another little village sat on a sandstone hill. At Al Uyaynah people kept sheep and goats and left more than 200 small clay objects. It was lived in for only a short time, in the same centuries.
ar: في وادٍ ينحدر إلى البحر الأحمر تتصل نحو 60 غرفة حجرية صغيرة كحبات في خيط. هذه وادي شرما 1. لبس أهلها حليًا من الصدف، وطحنوا طعامهم على الحجارة، وعادوا إليها موسمًا بعد موسم، قبل أكثر من 9,000 عام.

وعلى بعد نحو 100 كيلومتر، على الهضبة شمال تبوك، قامت قرية صغيرة أخرى على تل من الحجر الرملي. في العيينة ربّى الناس الأغنام والماعز وتركوا أكثر من 200 قطعة طينية صغيرة. وسُكنت لوقت قصير فقط، في القرون نفسها.

h2.en: Seen before: reading the seasons in sheep teeth
h2.ar: حدث من قبل: قراءة الفصول في أسنان الأغنام

en: A sheep’s tooth grows in bands, like the rings of a tree. Each band keeps a chemical trace of the water the animal drank and the plants it ate in that season.

In South Africa, Balasse and colleagues used these bands to test whether ancient herders took their flocks between the coast and the interior through the year. The teeth became a calendar and a map at once.
ar: يكبر سن الخروف في حلقات، كحلقات جذع الشجرة. وكل حلقة تحفظ أثرًا كيميائيًا للماء الذي شربه الحيوان والنباتات التي أكلها في ذلك الفصل.
وفي جنوب أفريقيا استخدم بالاس وزملاؤه هذه الحلقات لاختبار ما إذا كان الرعاة القدماء ينقلون قطعانهم بين الساحل والداخل خلال العام. فصارت الأسنان تقويمًا وخريطة معًا.

en: Put the two together. If the same herders spent one season in the Red Sea valleys and another on the plateau, walking through the Hisma mountains between, their animals’ teeth should show the switch, and shells from the sea should travel up to Al Uyaynah.
It could be otherwise. They may have been two different peoples, or one group that moved only once. The teeth and the shells can tell.
ar: اجمع الاثنين. إذا قضى الرعاة أنفسهم فصلًا في أودية البحر الأحمر وفصلًا على الهضبة، عابرين جبال حسمى بينهما، فينبغي أن تُظهر أسنان حيواناتهم هذا التبدّل، وأن تصعد أصداف البحر إلى العيينة.
وقد يكون الأمر غير ذلك. فربما كانا شعبين مختلفين، أو جماعة واحدة انتقلت مرة واحدة فقط. والأسنان والأصداف تستطيع أن تخبرنا.

spec.n: Maars as Water Gauges of the Hutaymah Field
spec.na: فوهات الماار مقاييسَ للماء في حقل الهتيمة
spec.te: Did water under the Hail plain decide where craters exploded and where a village grew?
spec.ta: هل حدّد الماء تحت سهول حائل أين انفجرت الفوهات وأين نشأت قرية؟
spec.desc: A connection between records on this map. The Pleistocene Hutaymah volcanic field near the Salma Mountains in Hail is less than 2 million years old and holds 77 volcanoes and 119 vent sites. Several of its craters are maars, formed when rising magma met groundwater and exploded. At Al Hutaymah a maar about 1.5 km wide and more than 200 m deep cut through an older scoria cone, recording a change from magmatic to water-driven (phreatomagmatic) eruptions. An Na’i erupted inside a basin among the granophyre rocks of the Salma mega-caldera, with repeated maars along fissures. Tabah is a wide maar partly filled with sediment, with a subsiding floor, and a village was built on its rim in pre-Islamic times. On the Red Sea coast, by contrast, only eight of the 160 vents counted at Harrat al-Birk are phreatomagmatic, near the shore and along Wadi Sabya. The idea: because a maar needs water, the maars of Hutaymah map where and when shallow groundwater lay under the plain, and the sediment trapped in their craters, as at Tabah, is both a record of those wetter times and a reason people settled there.
spec.sig: If true, the craters of Salma Geopark would be a gauge of past groundwater in northern Arabia, and the fill of Tabah crater a climate archive lying beneath a living village.
spec.ev: Hutaymah field: less than 2 Ma, about 900 km², 77 volcanoes and 119 vent sites; one maar gave an Ar–Ar age of 1.8 ± 0.5 Ma (Salma Geopark). Al Hutaymah: about 1.5 km wide and more than 200 m deep; cuts an older scoria cone; change from magmatic to phreatomagmatic eruptions as magma met groundwater (Németh 2026). An Na’i: inside an intra-mountain basin of the Salma mega-caldera; repeated maars along fissures; base-surge section about 1.5 km long and 30 m thick; inferred age about 1 Ma. Tabah: sediment-filled maar with a continuous tuff ring and visible subsidence of the crater floor; formed more than a million years ago; village on the rim since pre-Islamic times. Harrat al-Birk: 8 of 160 vents phreatomagmatic, including Surtseyan-style tuff cones near the coast and a maar–tuff ring along Wadi Sabya. From the map coordinates, Tabah lies about 9 km from Al Hutaymah and about 20 km from An Na’i.
spec.an: Lorenz (1986) explained the growth of maars and the diatremes beneath them as the result of repeated explosions where magma meets groundwater, so that a maar can only keep growing while the ground supplies water. In the Eifel of Germany, Sirocko and colleagues (2005) used sediment cores from maar lakes as a long, finely layered record of past climate.
spec.val: Map every vent of the Hutaymah field by eruption style (maar or scoria cone) and compare the styles with ground height, basins and fissures; date a sample of maars and cones by Ar–Ar to see whether the switch to maars clusters in time; core the sediment fill of Tabah crater and look for lake or playa layers, plant remains and datable material; check where Tabah village has drawn its water and whether the crater fill holds water today.
dlist: Rival explanation 1: the eruption style was set by the magma itself, its gas content and the speed of its rise, not by how much groundwater there was.
Rival explanation 2: water was always present in fractures of the old granite, so the maars record rock structure rather than wetter periods.
Rival explanation 3: Tabah village was built on the rim for its height, stone and defence, and the crater fill played no part in the choice.
refs: Németh, K. (2026). The Role of Phreatomagmatism in the Saudi Arabian Neogene–Quaternary Intra-plate Monogenetic Volcanism. In: Latest Advances in Volcanology – Volcanoes as Complex Geosystems. IntechOpen.
Salma UNESCO Global Geopark. Salma Geological Material for Website (geosite descriptions). NCVC.
Global Volcanism Program. Harrat al-Birk (231072). Volcanoes of the World. Smithsonian Institution.
Lorenz, V. (1986). On the growth of maars and diatremes and its relevance to the formation of tuff rings. Bulletin of Volcanology 48, 265–274.
Sirocko, F. et al. (2005). A late Eemian aridity pulse in central Europe during the last glacial inception. Nature 436, 833–836.
spec.se: Some craters near the Salma Mountains exploded because rising magma met water underground, and a village grew on the rim of one of them. Do the craters map where water once lay? Nobody has tested this yet.
spec.sa: انفجرت بعض الفوهات قرب جبال سلمى لأن الصهارة الصاعدة لاقت الماء تحت الأرض، ونشأت قرية على حافة إحداها. فهل ترسم هذه الفوهات خريطة للأماكن التي كان فيها الماء؟ لم يختبر أحد ذلك بعد.

spot.en: Born from five records on this map. Al Hutaymah, a maar more than 200 m deep, cut through an older dry cone when magma met groundwater; An Na’i erupted again and again along fissures in a mountain basin; Tabah’s wide crater filled with sediment and carries a village on its rim; Salma Geopark holds the whole field of 77 volcanoes. On the Red Sea coast, Harrat al-Birk has only eight such water-driven vents among 160.
spot.ar: وُلدت الفكرة من خمسة سجلات على هذه الخريطة: شقّت فوهة الهتيمة، وعمقها أكثر من 200 متر، مخروطًا جافًا أقدم منها حين لاقت الصهارة الماء الجوفي؛ وثارت فوهة النعي مرة بعد مرة على امتداد شقوق في حوض جبلي؛ وامتلأت فوهة طابة الواسعة بالرواسب وتحمل على حافتها قرية؛ ويضم جيوبارك سلمى الحقل كله بما فيه من 77 بركانًا. أما على ساحل البحر الأحمر فليس في حرة البرك من هذه الفتحات المائية الانفجار إلا ثماني فتحات من أصل 160.

tag.en: Some volcanoes near Salma exploded only because there was water underground
tag.ar: بعض براكين سلمى لم ينفجر إلا لأن الماء كان تحت الأرض

en: Near the Salma Mountains in Hail lies a field of 77 young volcanoes. Some are cones of cinders, called scoria cones. Others are maars: wide, deep holes blasted into the ground when rising magma met water underground and turned it into steam.
Al Hutaymah is more than 200 metres deep, and it cut right through an older, dry cone. Tabah is wide and partly filled with sediment, and a village has stood on its rim since before Islam.
ar: قرب جبال سلمى في حائل يمتد حقل فيه 77 بركانًا فتيًّا. بعضها مخاريط من الخَبَث البركاني، وبعضها الآخر فوهات من نوع «الماار»: حفر واسعة عميقة انفجرت في الأرض حين لاقت الصهارة الصاعدة الماء الجوفي فحوّلته بخارًا.
يزيد عمق فوهة الهتيمة على 200 متر، وقد شقّت مخروطًا أقدم منها كان جافًا. أما فوهة طابة فواسعة امتلأ بعضها بالرواسب، وعلى حافتها قرية قائمة منذ ما قبل الإسلام.

h2.en: Seen before: the crater lakes of the Eifel
h2.ar: حدث من قبل: بحيرات الفوهات في إيفل

en: In 1986 the volcanologist Volker Lorenz explained how maars grow: each time magma touches groundwater, an explosion digs the hole a little deeper. No water, no maar.
In the Eifel hills of Germany, old maar craters later filled with lakes. Sirocko and colleagues drilled into their mud and found fine layers that keep a long diary of past climate.
ar: شرح عالم البراكين فولكر لورنتس عام 1986 كيف تكبر فوهات الماار: كلما لامست الصهارة الماء الجوفي حفر انفجارٌ الحفرةَ أعمق قليلًا. فبلا ماء لا يكون ماار.
وفي تلال إيفل بألمانيا امتلأت فوهات ماار قديمة بالبحيرات. فحفر سيروكو وزملاؤه في طينها، فوجدوا طبقات دقيقة تحفظ سجلًا طويلًا لمناخ الماضي.

en: Put the two together. If maars need water, then the maars of Hutaymah show where water lay under the plain, and when. The mud inside Tabah crater may still hold a diary of those wetter times, right beneath the village.
It could be otherwise. The style of an eruption may depend on the magma, not the water, and the village may have chosen the rim for its height. Mapping the vents and drilling the crater can tell.
ar: اجمع الاثنين. إذا كانت فوهات الماار تحتاج إلى الماء، فإن فوهات الهتيمة تدل على المواضع التي كان فيها الماء تحت السهل، وعلى أزمنته. وربما ما زال طين فوهة طابة يحفظ سجل تلك الأزمنة الرطبة، تحت القرية مباشرة.
وقد يكون الأمر غير ذلك. فربما يتوقف نمط الثوران على الصهارة لا على الماء، وربما اختارت القرية الحافة لارتفاعها. ورسم خريطة الفتحات والحفر في الفوهة يستطيعان أن يخبرانا.

spec.n: The Mundafan Lake and the Cattle of Ḥimā
spec.te: Were Ḥimā’s cattle carved while the Empty Quarter’s lake still held water?
spec.ta: هل نُقشت أبقار حمى حين كانت بحيرة الربع الخالي ما تزال تحمل الماء؟
spec.desc: A connection between records on this map. Mundafan, on the south-western edge of the Rub’ al-Khali in Najran Province, was a lake again in the early Holocene, about 9,000–6,000 years ago; aurochs, camels, gazelles, hippopotamuses and ostriches lived around it, and Neolithic sites line its old shores. About 90 km to the west, the Ḥimā Cultural Area holds rock art carved over at least 7,000 years. At Najd Khayran, on Wadi Saad, thousands of petroglyphs include panels of bovids and people beside polished rock slides in front of a ‘waterfall’ feature. At ‘An Jamal, 6 km away, the site holds the most recent scientific evidence of surface water in the area, which helps estimate when the aquifer lowered and the region became desert. The Bir Hima wells have supplied travellers for about 3,000 years. The idea: the cattle panels of Ḥimā belong to the same wet phase as the Mundafan lake, and as the lake failed, life at Ḥimā moved from surface water and cattle to deep wells and caravans.
spec.sig: If true, the rock art of Ḥimā could be dated against the lake beds of Mundafan, and the two places together would show how south-western Arabia passed from green land to desert.
spec.ev: Mundafan (18.57 N, 45.33 E): lake high stands about 100,000 and 80,000 years ago and about 9,000–6,000 years ago; up to about 300 km² and 30 m deep; aurochs, camels, gazelles, hippopotamuses and ostriches; Middle Palaeolithic and Neolithic sites around the old shorelines (Crassard et al. 2013; Groucutt et al. 2015). Ḥimā: 34 rock-art sites carved over some 7,000 years; Bir Hima wells in use for about 3,000 years (UNESCO 2021). Najd Khayran: thousands of petroglyphs, bovids and human figures, four polished slides in front of a ‘waterfall’ feature. ‘An Jamal: 245 petroglyphs and 438 inscriptions; the most recent scientific evidence of surface water in the area; one inscription about 1,300–1,350 years old by micro-erosion calibration; a former caravan toll station (ICOMOS 2020). From the map coordinates, Mundafan lies about 90 km from Najd Khayran and ‘An Jamal, which are about 6 km apart.
spec.an: In northern Chad, Kröpelin and colleagues (2008) studied a continuous sediment core from Lake Yoa and showed that the Sahara around it dried gradually over the last 6,000 years, with its plant cover changing step by step rather than collapsing at once.
spec.val: Date the bovid panels at Najd Khayran and other Ḥimā sites by micro-erosion and by which carvings overlie which; date the surface-water evidence at ‘An Jamal; line both up with the dated high stands of Mundafan; check whether the earliest use of the Bir Hima wells follows the end of surface water.
dlist: Rival explanation 1: the cattle were carved long after the lake failed, by herders who watered their animals at wells.
Rival explanation 2: Ḥimā had its own water from the mountains and wadis, so its history need not follow Mundafan at all.
Rival explanation 3: the cattle in the art are symbols or memories, not a record of the animals kept at the time.

Groucutt, H.S. et al. (2015). Human occupation of the Arabian Empty Quarter during MIS 5: evidence from Mundafan Al-Buhayrah, Saudi Arabia. Quaternary Science Reviews 119, 116–135.
UNESCO World Heritage Centre. Ḥimā Cultural Area (ref. 1619), inscribed 2021.
ICOMOS (2020). Cultural Rock Arts in Ḥimā Najrān (Saudi Arabia), No 1619. Evaluation.
Kröpelin, S., Verschuren, D., Lézine, A.-M. et al. (2008). Climate-driven ecosystem succession in the Sahara: the past 6000 years. Science 320(5877), 765–768.
spec.se: About 90 km from the cattle carvings of Ḥimā, a lake full of life lay at the edge of the Empty Quarter 9,000–6,000 years ago. Were the cattle carved while the lake still held water? Nobody has tested this yet.
spec.sa: على بعد نحو 90 كيلومترًا من نقوش الأبقار في حمى، كانت على حافة الربع الخالي بحيرة تعجّ بالحياة قبل 9,000–6,000 عام. فهل نُقشت الأبقار حين كانت البحيرة ما تزال تحمل الماء؟ لم يختبر أحد ذلك بعد.

title.en: When the Desert Had a Lake

tag.en: The cattle on Ḥimā’s cliffs may remember a lake 90 km away
tag.ar: ربما تحفظ أبقار جروف حمى ذكرى بحيرة على بعد 90 كيلومترًا

en: At the edge of the Empty Quarter, where sand now reaches the horizon, there was once a lake called Mundafan. Between about 9,000 and 6,000 years ago it held water, and aurochs, camels, gazelles, ostriches and even hippopotamuses lived around it.
About 90 kilometres to the west, at Ḥimā, people carved thousands of pictures on the cliffs. At Najd Khayran, beside a ‘waterfall’ in the rock, the panels show cattle and people together.
ar: على حافة الربع الخالي، حيث تمتد الرمال اليوم إلى الأفق، كانت هناك بحيرة اسمها المندفن. وبين نحو 9,000 و6,000 عام مضت كانت مملوءة بالماء، وعاشت حولها الثيران البرية والجمال والغزلان والنعام، بل أفراس النهر أيضًا.
وعلى بعد نحو 90 كيلومترًا إلى الغرب، في حمى، نقش الناس آلاف الصور على الجروف. وفي نجد خيران، بجوار «شلال» في الصخر، تُظهر اللوحات أبقارًا وبشرًا معًا.

h2.en: Seen before: a lake that watched the Sahara dry
h2.ar: حدث من قبل: بحيرة شهدت جفاف الصحراء الكبرى

en: In northern Chad, Lake Yoa still holds water in the middle of the Sahara. Kröpelin and colleagues drilled into its mud and read it layer by layer.
The mud showed that the green Sahara did not vanish overnight. Over the last 6,000 years the plants around the lake changed step by step, and the land slowly turned to desert.
ar: في شمال تشاد ما تزال بحيرة يوا تحمل الماء وسط الصحراء الكبرى. حفر كروبلين وزملاؤه في طينها وقرؤوه طبقة طبقة.
فأظهر الطين أن الصحراء الخضراء لم تختفِ بين ليلة وضحاها. فعلى مدى الستة آلاف عام الأخيرة تبدّلت النباتات حول البحيرة خطوة خطوة، وتحولت الأرض ببطء إلى صحراء.

en: Put the two together. If the cattle of Ḥimā were carved while Mundafan still held water, their dates should match the lake. When the lake failed, the people of Ḥimā would have turned to deep wells, like the Bir Hima wells that have served travellers for about 3,000 years.
It could be otherwise. Herders may have kept cattle at wells long after the lake was gone. Dating the carvings can tell.
ar: اجمع الاثنين. إذا كانت أبقار حمى قد نُقشت حين كانت المندفن ما تزال تحمل الماء، فينبغي أن تتوافق تواريخها مع تواريخ البحيرة. وحين جفّت البحيرة لعلّ أهل حمى لجؤوا إلى الآبار العميقة، مثل آبار حمى التي تسقي المسافرين منذ نحو 3,000 عام.
وقد يكون الأمر غير ذلك. فربما ربّى الرعاة الأبقار على الآبار زمنًا طويلًا بعد زوال البحيرة. وتأريخ النقوش يستطيع أن يخبرنا.

spec.n: A Pilgrim Road Built on Older Places
spec.na: طريق حجّ قام على أماكن أقدم
spec.te: Did the Abbasid stations of Darb Zubaydah grow out of older pastures and mines?
spec.ta: هل نشأت محطات درب زبيدة العباسية من مراعٍ ومناجم أقدم منها؟
spec.desc: A connection between records on this map. Al-Rabadha, about 200 km north-east of Medina, began as a pasture reserve (hima) under the first caliphs, grew into a town in the Umayyad period and peaked in the early Abbasid era as a major station on Darb Zubaydah, the pilgrim road of roughly 1,300 km from Kufa to Makkah. Al-Neqrah, another station, lies in a flat agricultural area north of Jabal Ma‘dan and is linked with ancient copper mining as well as with pilgrim facilities such as the Al-Jafniyah Pool. Faid, which lay on the same road, is still surrounded by a historical protected rangeland, Faid Hema, of about 4,800 km², where a survey found 22 reptile species and suggested that control of grazing and hunting helped keep diversity high. At Al-Thulaimiya the road builders made a circular basin 32 m across. The idea: the stations were not placed only by distance and water, but grew on older places, protected pastures for the animals and mining settlements, and the himas that survive along the road are a living relic of that system.
spec.sig: If true, the Darb Zubaydah would be a map of older land use in central Arabia, and the surviving himas along it would deserve protection as part of the same heritage as the pools and stations.
spec.ev: Al-Rabadha (24.63 N, 41.30 E): pasture reserve under the first caliphs, a town in the Umayyad period, peak in the 9th century AD as a Darb Zubaydah station; fortified quarters, palaces, two mosques, a glass furnace, a circular reservoir (Al-Rashid 1986). Al-Neqrah (25.54 N, 41.59 E): station in a flat agricultural area north of Jabal Ma‘dan, linked with ancient copper mining and with the Al-Jafniyah Pool (UNESCO Tentative List 2022). Faid Hema: about 4,800 km² around Faid, which lay on the Kufa–Makkah road; 22 reptile species from 134 individuals in 2012–2013, richest at Jannin and poorest at an agricultural site (Alshammari & Ibrahim 2015). Al-Thulaimiya (29.62 N, 43.61 E): circular basin 32 m across with a two-layer wall and a staircase.
spec.an: In the Andes, Hyslop (1984) surveyed long stretches of the Inka road system and found that the imperial roads often followed and rebuilt older routes, so that a state network grew out of earlier local paths.
spec.val: Excavate below the Abbasid levels at stations such as Al-Neqrah and Al-Thulaimiya to see whether mining or pastoral use came first; date the copper workings near Al-Neqrah; compare the spacing of stations with distances to known himas, mines and water; survey plants and animals in the surviving himas along the road and in unprotected land nearby.
dlist: Rival explanation 1: stations were placed about a day’s march apart, wherever a pool or well could be built, with no regard for older places.
Rival explanation 2: the himas were set up after the road, to feed the pilgrims’ animals, not before it.
Rival explanation 3: Al-Rabadha is a special case, and most stations were new foundations with nothing older beneath them.

Al-Rashid, S. (1986). Al-Rabadhah: Portrait of Early Islamic Civilisation in Saudi Arabia. King Saud University, Riyadh.
Alshammari, A.M. & Ibrahim, A.A. (2015). Lizards and Snakes in the Historical Faid Protected Area (Faid Hema), Ha’il Region, Saudi Arabia. Herpetological Conservation and Biology 10(3), 1021–1029.
Hyslop, J. (1984). The Inka Road System. Academic Press, Orlando.
spec.se: One pilgrim station on Darb Zubaydah began as a protected pasture, another stood near ancient copper mines, and the town of Faid still lies inside a hima. Was the road built on older places? Nobody has tested this yet.
spec.sa: بدأت إحدى محطات الحج على درب زبيدة حِمًى للرعي، وقامت أخرى قرب مناجم نحاس قديمة، وما تزال بلدة فيد داخل حِمًى. فهل بُني الطريق على أماكن أقدم منه؟ لم يختبر أحد ذلك بعد.

spot.en: Born from four records on this map. Al-Rabadha began as a hima before it became a great station; Al-Neqrah stood near ancient copper mines; Faid still lies inside a hima of about 4,800 km² rich in reptiles; and Al-Thulaimiya shows the scale of the road’s water works. Pastures and mines first, the pilgrim road after?

title.en: The Road That Followed the Pastures

tag.en: Abbasid pilgrims may have walked from one old pasture or mine to the next
tag.ar: ربما سار حجاج العصر العباسي من مرعى قديم أو منجم قديم إلى آخر

en: Darb Zubaydah ran for about 1,300 kilometres from Kufa to Makkah. Along it the Abbasids built stations with great pools. At Al-Thulaimiya the round basin is 32 metres across, with a staircase leading down to the water.

But some stations were not new. Al-Rabadha began as a protected pasture, a hima, under the first caliphs. Al-Neqrah stood near ancient copper mines. And Faid is still surrounded by a hima of about 4,800 square kilometres.
ar: امتد درب زبيدة نحو 1,300 كيلومتر من الكوفة إلى مكة. وعلى طوله بنى العباسيون محطات ذات برك كبيرة. ففي الثليمية حوض مستدير قطره 32 مترًا، ينزل إليه درج حتى الماء.
لكن بعض المحطات لم تكن جديدة. فقد بدأت الربذة مرعًى محميًّا، أي حِمًى، في عهد الخلفاء الأوائل. وقامت النقرة قرب مناجم نحاس قديمة. وما تزال فيد يحيط بها حِمًى مساحته نحو 4,800 كيلومتر مربع.

h2.en: Seen before: the roads of the Inka

en: In the Andes of South America, the Inka built a vast network of roads. The archaeologist John Hyslop walked and mapped long stretches of it.
He found that the Inka often followed and rebuilt older paths. The great imperial road grew out of routes that local people had used long before.
ar: في جبال الأنديز بأمريكا الجنوبية بنى الإنكا شبكة طرق هائلة. ومشى عالم الآثار جون هايسلوب على أجزاء طويلة منها ورسم خرائطها.
فوجد أن الإنكا كثيرًا ما تتبّعوا مسالك أقدم وأعادوا بناءها. فقد نشأ الطريق الإمبراطوري الكبير من دروب سلكها السكان المحليون قبل ذلك بزمن طويل.

en: Put the two together. If Darb Zubaydah grew in the same way, its stations should stand on older places: pastures where camels could graze and mines where people already lived. Dig below the Abbasid floors, and something older should appear.
It could be otherwise. The stations may simply be a day’s march apart, wherever a pool could be built. Excavation can tell.
ar: اجمع الاثنين. إذا كان درب زبيدة قد نشأ بالطريقة نفسها، فينبغي أن تقوم محطاته على أماكن أقدم: مراعٍ ترعى فيها الإبل، ومناجم كان الناس يعيشون عندها من قبل. فإذا حفرنا تحت الأرضيات العباسية، فينبغي أن يظهر شيء أقدم.
وقد يكون الأمر غير ذلك. فربما كانت المحطات ببساطة على مسيرة يوم بعضها من بعض، حيثما أمكن بناء بركة. والتنقيب يستطيع أن يخبرنا.

spec.n: Reading the Rocks for Gold in Al-Bahah
spec.na: قراءة الصخور بحثًا عن الذهب في الباحة
spec.te: Did ancient miners find gold by following rust-coloured chert and quartz veins?
spec.ta: هل اهتدى المعدّنون القدماء إلى الذهب بتتبّع الصوان الصدئ وعروق الكوارتز؟
spec.desc: A connection between records on this map. In the southern Wadi Bidah district of the Arabian Shield near Al-Bahah, gold occurs in two kinds of rock. At Haffa Abith it lies in folded, iron-rich (ferruginous) chert with quartz veins and anomalous arsenic, and ancient open cuts and declines run more than 120 m down a steep hillside. At Bani Sar, about 10 km to the south, ancient open cuts, pits and shafts follow a quartz-vein system for more than 2,500 m inside a narrow diorite intrusion. Neither working is dated, but archaeological study of Al-Bahah’s mining landscape places Islamic-era mining in the region between the 7th and 12th centuries AD. Far to the north, the Darb Zubaydah station of Al-Neqrah is linked with ancient copper mining. The idea: the ancient miners of Al-Bahah prospected by eye, following rocks that stand out on the surface, rust-coloured chert and quartz veins, so their workings trace those outcrops, and mapping such outcrops from the air should reveal workings that are not yet recorded.
spec.sig: If true, geological maps and satellite images of iron-stained chert and quartz could become a tool for finding and protecting the ancient mines of south-western Arabia before development reaches them.
spec.ev: Haffa Abith (20.20 N, 41.45 E): gold in folded ferruginous chert within Precambrian carbonaceous schist, tuff, dolomitic marble, metabasalt and graywacke, tied to quartz veins, stringers and stockworks; low silver and base metals, anomalous arsenic; ancient open cuts and declines more than 120 m down the hillside; found by the survey in May 1979. Bani Sar (20.11 N, 41.44 E): ancient workings along a quartz-vein system for more than 2,500 m in a schistose diorite intrusion about 15 km long; investigated in April 1980 (Worl & Smith 1982). Islamic-era mining in the Al-Bahah region placed between the 7th and 12th centuries AD (Al-Zahrani 2014). Al-Neqrah is linked with ancient copper mining (UNESCO Tentative List 2022). From the map coordinates, the two Al-Bahah workings are about 10 km apart.
spec.an: In his worldwide survey of early mining, Craddock (1995) described how ancient prospectors located ore from signs on the surface, such as coloured and iron-stained outcrops, and then followed the ore bodies with open cuts, pits and shafts.
spec.val: Map iron-stained chert and quartz outcrops in the Wadi Bidah district from geological maps and satellite images; visit a sample of these outcrops and of other rocks and record every ancient cut, pit, crushing stone or waste heap; compare how often each kind of rock carries workings; date charcoal and debris from the Bani Sar and Haffa Abith workings; test soils at processing places for arsenic to tell chert ore from vein ore.
dlist: Rival explanation 1: Islamic-era miners simply reopened older workings, so the pattern reflects earlier prospectors rather than their own reading of the rocks.
Rival explanation 2: gold was first found in wadi gravels and traced uphill, so the workings follow streams rather than the colour of the outcrops.
Rival explanation 3: modern geologists found these sites by the same visible rocks, so the link between outcrops and workings is a bias of where people have looked.

Al-Zahrani, A.A.A. (2014). Mining in Al-Baha Region, South-Western Saudi Arabia in Islamic-Era: The Archaeology of Asham. PhD thesis, University of York.
UNESCO World Heritage Centre (2022). The Hajj Pilgrimage Routes: The Darb Zubaydah (Saudi Arabia, Iraq). Tentative List ref. 6577.
Craddock, P.T. (1995). Early Metal Mining and Production. Edinburgh University Press, Edinburgh.
spec.se: Near Al-Bahah, ancient miners dug for gold in rust-coloured chert and along quartz veins. Did they find it by reading the colours of the rocks? Nobody has tested this yet.
spec.sa: قرب الباحة حفر المعدّنون القدماء بحثًا عن الذهب في صوان بلون الصدأ وعلى امتداد عروق الكوارتز. فهل اهتدوا إليه بقراءة ألوان الصخور؟ لم يختبر أحد ذلك بعد.

spot.en: Born from three records on this map. At Haffa Abith, ancient cuts run more than 120 m down a hillside in iron-rich chert; about 10 km away at Bani Sar, workings follow quartz veins for more than 2,500 m; and far to the north, Al-Neqrah on the pilgrim road is linked with ancient copper mining. Two kinds of rock, one way of searching?

pred.ar: ستحمل مكاشف الصوان المصبوغ بالحديد والكوارتز في منطقة وادي بيدة حفريات قديمة أكثر بكثير من الصخور الأخرى، وسيقود رسم خرائط هذه المكاشف من صور الأقمار الصناعية إلى حفريات لم تُسجَّل بعد، وستقع تواريخ الحفريات المعروفة بين القرنين السابع والثاني عشر الميلاديين.

test.en: Map the outcrops, visit a random sample of them and of other rocks, record every ancient working, and date the debris in the known mines.

wrong.en: If ancient workings are no more common on chert and quartz outcrops than on other rocks, or new workings turn up mainly in wadi gravels, the reading-the-rocks idea fails.

tag.en: The gold miners of Al-Bahah may have read the colours of the hills
tag.ar: ربما قرأ معدّنو الذهب في الباحة ألوان التلال

en: In the hills north of Al-Bahah, miners of long ago left long scars in the rock. At Haffa Abith their cuts run more than 120 metres down a steep slope, through layers of chert stained by iron. Gold hides in that chert.

About ten kilometres away at Bani Sar, the old workings follow quartz veins for more than 2,500 metres. Nobody has dated them yet, but mining in this region was active between the 7th and 12th centuries AD.
ar: في التلال شمال الباحة ترك معدّنون عاشوا قبل زمن طويل ندوبًا طويلة في الصخر. ففي حفة عابث تمتد حفرياتهم أكثر من 120 مترًا على منحدر شديد، عبر طبقات من الصوان صبغها الحديد. وفي ذلك الصوان يختبئ الذهب.
وعلى بعد نحو عشرة كيلومترات في بني سار تتبع الحفريات القديمة عروق الكوارتز لأكثر من 2,500 متر. لم يؤرّخها أحد بعد، لكن التعدين في هذه المنطقة كان نشطًا بين القرنين السابع والثاني عشر الميلاديين.

en: Long before chemistry laboratories, miners had to find ore with their eyes. The archaeologist Paul Craddock gathered evidence of early mining from around the world.
He described how ancient prospectors looked for signs on the surface, such as rocks stained by iron, and then chased the ore into the ground with cuts, pits and shafts.
ar: قبل مختبرات الكيمياء بزمن طويل كان على المعدّنين أن يعثروا على الخام بأعينهم. وقد جمع عالم الآثار بول كرادوك شواهد التعدين المبكر من أنحاء العالم.
ووصف كيف كان المنقّبون القدماء يبحثون عن علامات على سطح الأرض، كالصخور التي صبغها الحديد، ثم يتتبّعون الخام في باطن الأرض بالخنادق والحفر والآبار.

en: Put the two together. If the miners of Al-Bahah read the colours of the hills, their workings should follow the rust-coloured chert and the quartz veins. Then satellite pictures of those rocks could point to mines that nobody has recorded yet.
It could be otherwise. The miners may have traced gold uphill from the wadis, or reopened much older mines. A walk along the outcrops can tell.
ar: اجمع الاثنين. إذا كان معدّنو الباحة يقرؤون ألوان التلال، فينبغي أن تتبع حفرياتهم الصوان الصدئ وعروق الكوارتز. وعندئذ تستطيع صور الأقمار الصناعية لهذه الصخور أن تدل على مناجم لم يسجلها أحد بعد.
وقد يكون الأمر غير ذلك. فربما تتبّع المعدّنون الذهب صعودًا من الأودية، أو أعادوا فتح مناجم أقدم بكثير. وجولة على امتداد المكاشف تستطيع أن تخبرنا.

refs: Worl & Smith (1982). Reconnaissance investigations of ancient gold mines in the southern part of the Wadi Bidah District. USGS Open-File Report 82-789.

Craddock (1995). Early Metal Mining and Production. Edinburgh University Press.

spec.n: A Cooler North for Red Sea Turtles?
spec.na: هل الشمال الأبرد ملاذ لسلاحف البحر الأحمر؟
spec.te: Will hot sand push turtle nesting north along the Saudi Red Sea coast?
spec.ta: هل سيدفع الرمل الحار تعشيش السلاحف شمالًا على الساحل السعودي للبحر الأحمر؟
spec.desc: A connection between records on this map. At Ras Baridi, about 70 km north of Yanbu, the number of nesting green turtles rose from 14–110 females a year in 1982–1995 to 330 in 2019, and tracking there showed nesting success above 0.8 when the daytime sand-surface temperature was below 37 °C, falling below 0.4 above 47 °C. Mashabah Island, off Al Wajh further north, held 113 nesting females in 2018 and 179 in 2019. In the south, the Four Sisters Islands off Al-Lith are the largest recorded turtle nesting site in Saudi waters, with more than 2,500 nests of green and hawksbill turtles, and the Farasan Islands also host both species; in nearby Baish Bay, seawater reached 35–37 °C during a 2017 study. The idea: because nesting success falls so steeply with sand temperature, if the southern beaches run hotter, warming will hit the southern rookeries first, and the northern beaches and islands of the Saudi coast will become a growing refuge for Red Sea turtles.
spec.sig: If true, northern rookeries such as Mashabah Island and Ras Baridi would matter more with every decade, and sand-temperature monitoring in the south would give an early warning.
spec.ev: Ras Baridi (24.27 N, 37.63 E): 14–110 nesting females in 1982–1995, 178 in 2018 and 330 in 2019, with an upward trend; mean re-nesting interval 10.8 days; nesting success above 0.8 below 37 °C daytime sand-surface temperature and below 0.4 above 47 °C (Shimada et al. 2021). Mashabah Island (25.65 N, 36.45 E): 113 nesting females in 2018 and 179 in 2019. Four Sisters Islands (19.79 N, 39.95 E): more than 2,500 nests of green and hawksbill turtles, announced in November 2024 (SHAMS; Tanabe et al. 2023). Farasan Islands (16.7 N, 42.0 E): green and hawksbill turtles. Baish Bay (17.35 N, 42.32 E): seawater 35–37 °C between April and July 2017 (Abrogueña et al. 2022). From the map coordinates, Mashabah Island and the Farasan Islands are about 1,150 km apart.
spec.an: On Australia’s Great Barrier Reef, Jensen and colleagues (2018) showed that green turtles hatched on the warmer northern beaches were almost all female, while those from the cooler southern beaches were not, so that a temperature gradient along one coast gave one turtle population very different futures.
spec.val: Place temperature loggers on the sand surface and at nest depth at Mashabah Island, Ras Baridi, the Four Sisters and Farasan through whole nesting seasons; record nesting success and hatchling sex ratios at each; compare trends in nest counts between northern and southern sites using the same survey methods; follow tagged females to see whether any shift between beaches.
dlist: Rival explanation 1: nest counts follow protection and disturbance, such as lights, building and egg collection, not temperature.
Rival explanation 2: turtles return to the beaches where they hatched, so they will not shift north even if the south warms.
Rival explanation 3: the southern islands stay cool enough through wind, shade or moist sand, so the north–south difference is small.
refs: Shimada, T. et al. (2021). Distribution and temporal trends in the abundance of nesting sea turtles in the Red Sea. Biological Conservation 261, 109235.

Shimada, T., Duarte, C.M., Al-Suwailem, A.M., Tanabe, L.K. & Meekan, M.G. (2021). Satellite tracking reveals nesting patterns, site fidelity, and potential impacts of warming on major green turtle rookeries in the Red Sea. Frontiers in Marine Science 8, 633814.
Tanabe, L.K., Cochran, J.E.M. & Berumen, M.L. (2023). Inter-nesting, migration, and foraging behaviors of green turtles (Chelonia mydas) in the central-southern Red Sea. Scientific Reports 13, 11222.
Abrogueña, J.B.R. et al. (2022). The impact of inundation and sandstorms on the growth and survival of the mangrove Avicennia marina seedlings in the southern Red Sea. Scientia Marina 86(3), e041.

Jensen, M.P., Allen, C.D., Eguchi, T., Bell, I.P., LaCasella, E.L., Hilton, W.A., Hof, C.A.M. & Dutton, P.H. (2018). Environmental warming and feminization of one of the largest sea turtle populations in the world. Current Biology 28(1), 154–159.
spec.se: At Ras Baridi, turtle nests fail more often when the sand gets very hot. As the coast warms, will the northern beaches become the turtles’ refuge? Nobody has tested this yet.
spec.sa: في رأس بريدي تفشل أعشاش السلاحف أكثر حين يشتد حرّ الرمل. فمع ارتفاع حرارة الساحل، هل تصبح الشواطئ الشمالية ملاذًا للسلاحف؟ لم يختبر أحد ذلك بعد.

spot.en: Born from five records on this map. At Ras Baridi nesting females rose to 330 in 2019, and nests failed more often in hot sand; Mashabah Island to the north is a newly recognised rookery; the Four Sisters and Farasan in the south hold the largest nesting site and both green and hawksbill turtles; and Baish Bay’s seawater reached 35–37 °C.
spot.ar: وُلدت الفكرة من خمسة سجلات على هذه الخريطة: ارتفع عدد الإناث المعشِّشة في رأس بريدي إلى 330 عام 2019، وكانت الأعشاش تفشل أكثر في الرمل الحار؛ وجزيرة مشابه في الشمال موقع تعشيش لم يُعرف إلا حديثًا؛ وفي الجنوب تضم جزر الأخوات الأربع وفرسان أكبر موقع للتعشيش والسلاحف الخضراء وصقرية المنقار معًا؛ وبلغت حرارة مياه خليج بيش 35–37 درجة مئوية.

test.en: Log sand temperatures and nesting success at northern and southern rookeries with the same methods, and compare the long-term trends in nest counts.

tag.en: As the sand heats up, Red Sea turtles may find their future in the north
tag.ar: مع اشتداد حرارة الرمل، ربما تجد سلاحف البحر الأحمر مستقبلها في الشمال

en: On a beach north of Yanbu called Ras Baridi, green turtles crawl ashore to lay their eggs. In 2019 scientists counted 330 mothers there, many more than in the 1980s.

They also tracked the turtles and measured the sand. When the surface was cooler than 37 °C, most nesting attempts succeeded. When it was hotter than 47 °C, most failed. Hot sand is bad news for turtles.
ar: على شاطئ شمال ينبع اسمه رأس بريدي تزحف السلاحف الخضراء إلى البر لتضع بيضها. وفي عام 2019 أحصى العلماء هناك 330 أمًّا، وهو عدد أكبر بكثير مما كان في ثمانينيات القرن الماضي.
وتتبّعوا السلاحف أيضًا وقاسوا حرارة الرمل. فحين كان السطح أبرد من 37 درجة مئوية نجحت معظم محاولات التعشيش، وحين تجاوزت حرارته 47 درجة فشل معظمها. فالرمل الحار نذير سوء للسلاحف.

h2.en: Seen before: a reef with a hot north
h2.ar: حدث من قبل: شعاب شمالها حار

en: Along Australia’s Great Barrier Reef, green turtles nest on beaches from the cooler south to the hotter north. For turtles, the warmth of the sand decides whether a hatchling becomes male or female.
Jensen and colleagues found that young turtles from the warm northern beaches were almost all female, while those from the cooler south were not. One coast, two very different futures.
ar: على امتداد الحاجز المرجاني العظيم في أستراليا تعشّش السلاحف الخضراء على شواطئ تمتد من الجنوب الأبرد إلى الشمال الأشد حرارة. ودفء الرمل عند السلاحف هو ما يحدد أذكرًا يكون الصغير أم أنثى.
ووجد جنسن وزملاؤه أن صغار السلاحف القادمة من الشواطئ الشمالية الدافئة كانت كلها تقريبًا إناثًا، بخلاف صغار الجنوب الأبرد. ساحل واحد، ومستقبلان مختلفان تمامًا.

en: Put the two together. If the beaches of the southern Saudi coast are hotter than those of the north, nests at the Four Sisters and Farasan may fail more often as the climate warms, and northern beaches like Ras Baridi and Mashabah Island may become the turtles’ refuge.
It could be otherwise. Turtles return to the beach where they hatched, and nest counts may depend more on people than on heat. Thermometers in the sand can tell.
ar: اجمع الاثنين. إذا كانت شواطئ الساحل السعودي الجنوبي أشد حرارة من شواطئ الشمال، فقد تفشل الأعشاش في جزر الأخوات الأربع وفرسان أكثر مع ارتفاع حرارة المناخ، وقد تصبح الشواطئ الشمالية مثل رأس بريدي وجزيرة مشابه ملاذًا للسلاحف.
وقد يكون الأمر غير ذلك. فالسلاحف تعود إلى الشاطئ الذي فقست فيه، وربما تتوقف أعداد الأعشاش على البشر أكثر مما تتوقف على الحرارة. وموازين الحرارة المغروسة في الرمل تستطيع أن تخبرنا.

refs: Shimada et al. (2021). Satellite tracking reveals nesting patterns, site fidelity, and potential impacts of warming on major green turtle rookeries in the Red Sea. Frontiers in Marine Science 8.
