spec.n: The Asir Magpie and the Water That Never Dries
spec.na: عقعق عسير والماء الذي لا يجف
spec.te: Does the rare Asir magpie need junipers alone, or junipers beside water that never dries?
spec.ta: هل يحتاج عقعق عسير النادر إلى العرعر وحده، أم إلى عرعر بجوار ماء لا يجف؟
spec.desc: A connection between records on this map. The Asir magpie (Pica pica asirensis), a magpie found only in the Asir highlands, lives mainly in upland valleys at 1,850–3,000 m, and its breeding population has been estimated at a minimum of 135 pairs; habitat loss and juniper dieback are its main threats. At Raydah, junipers grow between 2,500 and 3,000 m where monsoon cloud brings moisture, and the escarpment beside Jabal Sawda falls from 2,700 to 1,600 m in less than 3 km, with permanent streams and frequent cloud. Shallal ad-Dahna, at about 2,100–2,700 m in juniper and acacia scrub, has one of the few permanent waterfalls in Saudi Arabia and supports the magpie. At Al Mehfar near Tanomah, at 1,950 m in the juniper zone, birds and nests were recorded between 2014 and 2016. Asir National Park protects Juniperus procera woodland above about 1,600 m. The idea: the magpie depends not on juniper alone but on juniper kept moist by cloud and lasting water, so its remaining territories should cluster where trees and permanent water meet, and failing streams, more than tree loss alone, will decide where it disappears.
spec.sig: If true, protecting the streams, springs and cloud-fed slopes of Asir would matter as much for the magpie as protecting the trees, and water maps could guide the search for pairs not yet found.
spec.ev: Asir magpie: upland valleys at 1,850–3,000 m; breeding population estimated at a minimum of 135 pairs; threats from tourism, development and juniper dieback (Babbington 2016). Raydah (18.2 N, 42.4 E): densest juniper woodland in the kingdom, junipers at 2,500–3,000 m with monsoon cloud; shelters the magpie. Jabal Sawda: 3,015 m; the adjoining Raydah escarpment falls from 2,700 to 1,600 m in less than 3 km, with permanent streams, frequent cloud and largely intact Juniperus excelsa forest. Shallal ad-Dahna (18.91 N, 42.23 E): 2,100–2,700 m, juniper and acacia scrub, one of the few permanent waterfalls in Saudi Arabia; supports the magpie and frogs and toads that need permanent water. Al Mehfar (18.96 N, 42.13 E): 1,950 m in the juniper zone; one bird in January 2014, a nest in May 2014, two juveniles in July 2014, four birds in July 2015, four nests (two new) in June 2016. Asir National Park: Juniperus procera woodland above about 1,600 m.
spec.an: At Monteverde in Costa Rica, Pounds, Fogden and Campbell (1999) linked a rise in the cloud base and more dry-season days without mist to changes in the birds, frogs and lizards of a tropical cloud forest, including birds from lower slopes moving upslope.
spec.val: Map all known and historical Asir magpie territories; measure for each the distance to permanent water (streams, springs, waterfalls), the frequency of cloud and the health of the junipers; compare them with randomly chosen juniper patches at the same heights; follow nest occupancy at sites such as Al Mehfar against stream flow from year to year.
dlist: Rival explanation 1: the magpie needs tall, healthy junipers for nesting, and permanent water happens to occur in the same places by chance.
Rival explanation 2: disturbance from tourism and development, not water, decides where the birds survive.
Rival explanation 3: the magpie may feed largely on terraces and fields near villages, so human land use matters more than wild water.
refs: Babbington, J. (2016). Update on the status and occurrence of Arabian Magpie Pica pica asirensis in Saudi Arabia. Sandgrouse 38, 146–151.

Key Biodiversity Areas Partnership. Raydah escarpment (KBA 8282) factsheet.

spec.se: The rare Asir magpie lives among junipers, but several of its known homes also have permanent streams or a waterfall that never stops. Does it need water as much as trees? Nobody has tested this yet.
spec.sa: يعيش عقعق عسير النادر بين أشجار العرعر، لكن عددًا من مواطنه المعروفة فيها أيضًا جداول دائمة أو شلال لا يتوقف. فهل يحتاج إلى الماء بقدر حاجته إلى الأشجار؟ لم يختبر أحد ذلك بعد.

spot.en: Born from five records on this map. The Asir magpie, with at least 135 pairs, lives in upland valleys of 1,850–3,000 m; Raydah’s cloud-fed junipers and the escarpment beside Jabal Sawda have permanent streams; Shallal ad-Dahna has one of the few permanent waterfalls in the kingdom and supports the bird; Al Mehfar near Tanomah held nests in 2014–2016; and Asir National Park protects juniper woodland above about 1,600 m.
spot.ar: وُلدت الفكرة من خمسة سجلات على هذه الخريطة: يعيش عقعق عسير، ولا يقل عدده عن 135 زوجًا، في أودية مرتفعة بين 1,850 و3,000 متر؛ وفي عرعر ريدة الذي تسقيه الغيوم وفي المنحدر المجاور لجبل السودة جداول دائمة؛ وفي شلال الدهناء أحد الشلالات الدائمة القليلة في المملكة، وهو موطن لهذا الطائر؛ وفي منتزه المحفار قرب تنومة سُجّلت أعشاش بين 2014 و2016؛ ويحمي منتزه عسير الوطني غابات العرعر فوق نحو 1,600 متر.

pred.en: Known Asir magpie territories will lie closer to permanent streams, springs or waterfalls than juniper patches of the same height that hold no magpies, and nest sites will be abandoned where streams fail even when the trees still stand.

test.en: Compare magpie territories with random juniper patches for distance to permanent water and cloud cover, and follow nest occupancy against stream flow over several years.
test.ar: مقارنة مناطق العقعق ببقع عرعر مختارة عشوائيًا من حيث القرب من الماء الدائم وتكرار الغيوم، ومتابعة إشغال الأعشاش مقارنةً بجريان الجداول على مدى عدة سنوات.

wrong.en: If magpie territories are no closer to permanent water than empty juniper patches, or the birds stay on where streams dry up, the water idea fails.

tag.en: Arabia’s rarest magpie may need running water as much as trees
tag.ar: ربما يحتاج أندر عقعق في الجزيرة العربية إلى الماء الجاري بقدر حاجته إلى الأشجار

en: High in the Asir mountains lives a bird found nowhere else: the Asir magpie. Perhaps only about 135 pairs remain, in valleys between 1,850 and 3,000 metres, among juniper trees fed by the clouds.

Its homes share something besides junipers. Beside Jabal Sawda the escarpment has permanent streams and frequent cloud. Shallal ad-Dahna has one of the few waterfalls in Saudi Arabia that never stops flowing.
ar: في أعالي جبال عسير يعيش طائر لا يوجد في أي مكان آخر: عقعق عسير. وربما لم يبقَ منه إلا نحو 135 زوجًا، في أودية بين 1,850 و3,000 متر، بين أشجار عرعر تسقيها الغيوم.
ولمواطنه شيء مشترك غير العرعر. فالمنحدر المجاور لجبل السودة فيه جداول دائمة وغيوم متكررة. وفي شلال الدهناء أحد الشلالات القليلة في المملكة التي لا يتوقف جريانها.

h2.en: Seen before: the cloud forest that lost its mist
h2.ar: حدث من قبل: غابة سحابية فقدت ضبابها

en: At Monteverde in Costa Rica, a forest grows inside the clouds. Pounds and his colleagues followed its animals for years.

They found that as the clouds rose higher and the dry season brought more days without mist, the animals changed: frogs and lizards declined, and birds from lower slopes moved up the mountain. The mist mattered as much as the trees.
ar: في مونتيفيردي بكوستاريكا تنمو غابة داخل الغيوم. وقد تابع باوندز وزملاؤه حيواناتها سنوات طويلة.
فوجدوا أنه حين ارتفعت الغيوم وجلب موسم الجفاف أيامًا أكثر بلا ضباب تغيّرت الحيوانات: تراجعت الضفادع والسحالي، وصعدت طيور المنحدرات الدنيا إلى أعلى الجبل. فقد كان للضباب من الأهمية ما للأشجار.

en: Put the two together. If the Asir magpie needs the moisture of cloud and running water as well as junipers, its nests should cluster where trees and lasting water meet, and it should leave places where the streams dry up, even if the trees survive.
It could be otherwise. The birds may simply need tall, healthy trees, or quiet away from people. Mapping the water around every nest can tell.
ar: اجمع الاثنين. إذا كان عقعق عسير يحتاج إلى رطوبة الغيوم والماء الجاري إلى جانب العرعر، فينبغي أن تتجمع أعشاشه حيث تلتقي الأشجار بالماء الدائم، وأن يرحل عن الأماكن التي تجف فيها الجداول، حتى لو بقيت الأشجار حية.
وقد يكون الأمر غير ذلك. فربما لا يحتاج الطائر إلا إلى أشجار طويلة سليمة، أو إلى الهدوء بعيدًا عن الناس. ورسم خريطة الماء حول كل عش يستطيع أن يخبرنا.

spec.n: Walls Against the Flood: Jurash and the Ancient Dams
spec.na: جدران في وجه السيل: جرش والسدود القديمة
spec.te: Did the floods that buried Jurash also fill the silt behind the great stone dams?
spec.ta: هل ملأت السيول التي دفنت جرش الطميَ خلف السدود الحجرية العظيمة أيضًا؟
spec.desc: A connection between three records on this map. Jurash, on Wadi Bisha in Asir, was a fortified settlement from about the 3rd century BC to the early 7th century AD and then an Early Islamic town of the 7th to early 11th century AD, and geological study documents repeated destructive flash floods from Wadi Bisha that buried and reshaped its deposits. In Wadi Thumalah, about 30 km south-west of Taif, Sadd Samallaqi, 212 m long and 25 m high, was probably built in the reign of Mu‘awiya, according to a partly illegible inscription. In Harrat Khaybar, Sadd al-Bint, a basalt dam about 30 m high, is described as pre-Islamic or Early Islamic, and almost a third of it has been breached. The idea: the dams were built in, and against, the same era of violent floods that kept burying Jurash, so the silt trapped behind them should hold thick flood layers of the same centuries as the flood deposits at Jurash.
spec.sig: If true, the ancient dams of western Arabia would be more than monuments: their trapped silt would be a dated diary of past floods across hundreds of kilometres, and Jurash would show what those same floods did to a town that had no dam.
spec.ev: Jurash (18.20 N, 42.82 E): pre-Islamic fortified settlement c. 3rd century BC – early 7th century AD; Early Islamic town 7th – early 11th century AD with houses, workshops and two successive mosques; repeated destructive flash floods from Wadi Bisha buried and reshaped the deposits (Harrell 2025). Sadd Samallaqi (21.13 N, 40.51 E): 212 m long, 25 m high and 10 m wide at the top, between two mountains in Wadi Thumalah; a partly illegible inscription suggests the reign of Mu‘awiya ibn Abi Sufyan. Sadd al-Bint (25.49 N, 39.36 E): black basalt, about 30 m high, once spanning about 200 m of a deep, steep valley; about 135 m survive after almost a third was breached; yellow mortar plaster on the upstream face for waterproofing; dated only as pre-Islamic or Early Islamic. Both dams belong to the UNESCO Tentative List entry Water Management in Saudi Arabia: The Ancient Dams (2023). Sadd Samallaqi lies about 400 km and Sadd al-Bint about 880 km from Jurash, so any shared flood signal would have to be regional.
spec.an: At Marib in Yemen, the fields watered by the great ancient dam were raised over the centuries by the silt each flood left behind, building deposits many metres thick; researchers have read those layers to trace how the oasis was irrigated and how its floods changed through time.
spec.val: Core or trench the silt trapped behind Sadd Samallaqi and Sadd al-Bint down to bedrock; identify individual flood layers by grain size and bedding; date them by luminescence and by radiocarbon on charcoal or plant remains; date the flood deposits that bury the Early Islamic levels at Jurash in the same way; compare the three records century by century.
dlist: Rival explanation 1: the dams were built when people, travellers or rulers needed stored water and could pay for it, in an ordinary climate; floods had nothing special to do with the timing.
Rival explanation 2: the floods at Jurash came from storms over the Wadi Bisha catchment alone and say nothing about valleys hundreds of kilometres away.
Rival explanation 3: the silt behind the dams was flushed out when they were breached or cleaned, so it no longer holds a record that can be compared.

spec.se: Floods from Wadi Bisha kept burying the town of Jurash, while in roughly the same centuries great stone dams rose across valleys near Taif and Khaybar. Does the silt behind the dams record the same floods? Nobody has tested this yet.
spec.sa: ظلّت سيول وادي بيشة تدفن بلدة جرش، وفي قرون متقاربة ارتفعت سدود حجرية عظيمة عبر الأودية قرب الطائف وخيبر. فهل يسجّل الطمي خلف السدود السيولَ نفسها؟ لم يختبر أحد ذلك بعد.

spot.en: Born from three records on this map. Jurash, a town of the 3rd century BC to the early 11th century AD, was buried again and again by flash floods; Sadd Samallaqi, near Taif, was probably built in the reign of Mu‘awiya; and Sadd al-Bint, in Harrat Khaybar, is pre-Islamic or Early Islamic. Floods and dams kept turning up in the same stretch of centuries.
spot.ar: وُلدت الفكرة من ثلاثة سجلات على هذه الخريطة: فجرش، البلدة التي عُمرت من القرن الثالث قبل الميلاد إلى أوائل القرن الحادي عشر الميلادي، دفنتها السيول الجارفة مرة بعد مرة؛ ويُرجَّح أن سد السملقي قرب الطائف بُني في عهد معاوية؛ ويعود سد البنت في حرة خيبر إلى ما قبل الإسلام أو إلى صدر الإسلام. فقد ظلّت السيول والسدود تظهر في الحقبة نفسها من القرون.

tag.en: A buried town and two ancient dams may share the same floods
tag.ar: ربما تتقاسم بلدة مدفونة وسدّان قديمان السيولَ نفسها

en: In Asir, on the banks of Wadi Bisha, lies Jurash. For more than a thousand years people lived there, first behind walls of giant granite blocks, later in an Early Islamic town with houses, workshops and two mosques, one built after the other.

But Wadi Bisha did not always flow gently. Geologists found that flash floods roared down it again and again, burying and reshaping the town. Far to the north, near Taif and Khaybar, people of roughly the same centuries built huge stone dams across their valleys.
ar: في عسير، على ضفاف وادي بيشة، تقع جرش. عاش الناس فيها أكثر من ألف عام: أولًا خلف أسوار من كتل جرانيتية عملاقة، ثم في بلدة إسلامية مبكرة فيها بيوت وورش ومسجدان بُني أحدهما بعد الآخر.

لكن وادي بيشة لم يكن يجري هادئًا دائمًا. فقد وجد الجيولوجيون أن السيول الجارفة اندفعت فيه مرة بعد مرة، فدفنت البلدة وغيّرت معالمها. وبعيدًا في الشمال، قرب الطائف وخيبر، بنى أناس عاشوا في قرون متقاربة سدودًا حجرية ضخمة عبر أوديتهم.

h2.en: Seen before: the silt of Marib

en: At Marib in Yemen stood one of the most famous dams of the ancient world. Every flood it caught carried silt, and the silt spread over the fields the dam watered.
Over the centuries those layers built up many metres thick. Researchers have read them like the pages of a diary, to learn how the oasis was watered and how its floods changed through time.
ar: في مأرب باليمن قام واحد من أشهر سدود العالم القديم. وكان كل سيل يحتجزه يحمل طميًا، فينتشر الطمي فوق الحقول التي يسقيها السد.
وعلى مرّ القرون تراكمت تلك الطبقات حتى بلغ سمكها أمتارًا كثيرة. وقد قرأها الباحثون كما تُقرأ صفحات مذكّرات، ليعرفوا كيف كانت الواحة تُسقى وكيف تغيّرت سيولها عبر الزمن.

en: Put the pieces together. If a time of violent floods swept western Arabia, the silt piled up behind Sadd Samallaqi and Sadd al-Bint should hold thick flood layers from the same centuries as the floods that buried Jurash.

It could be otherwise. Dams may simply be built when people can afford them, and storms over one valley say little about another hundreds of kilometres away. Dating the silt in all three places can tell.
ar: اجمع القطع معًا. إذا كان زمنٌ من السيول العنيفة قد اجتاح غرب الجزيرة العربية، فينبغي أن يحمل الطمي المتراكم خلف سد السملقي وسد البنت طبقات سيول سميكة من القرون نفسها التي دفنت فيها السيول جرش.

وقد يكون الأمر غير ذلك. فربما تُبنى السدود ببساطة حين يقدر الناس على بنائها، والعواصف فوق وادٍ واحد لا تخبرنا الكثير عن وادٍ آخر على بعد مئات الكيلومترات. وتأريخ الطمي في الأماكن الثلاثة يستطيع أن يحسم الأمر.

spec.n: The Last Mangroves: Does Shelter Draw the Northern Limit?
spec.na: آخر أشجار القرم: هل يرسم الاحتماء الحدَّ الشمالي؟
spec.te: Do the northernmost mangroves of the Red Sea survive only where the coast shelters them?
spec.ta: هل لا تبقى أشجار القرم الأبعد شمالًا في البحر الأحمر إلا حيث يحميها الساحل؟
spec.desc: A connection between three records on this map. Near Duba, at about 27°25′N, the grey mangrove Avicennia marina reaches its northern limit on the Saudi Red Sea coast, and the northernmost of ten mangrove stations sampled between Duba and Al-Birk lies in an inland lagoon away from human activities. Farther south, the Al Wajh lagoon, 2,081 km² enclosed by a barrier reef with 92 islands, holds mangroves, seagrass beds and coral reefs whose corals are among the most heat-tolerant known. Near Al-Lith, Qishran Bay is almost enclosed by a long, narrow island and eight smaller islets, most of them fringed by Avicennia mangroves. The idea: towards the cooler, saltier north, mangroves can hold on only where reefs, islands or enclosed lagoons give them calm, sheltered water, so the northern stands should lie almost entirely in such places, while farther south more of them grow on open shores.
spec.sig: If true, the shape of the coast, and not only the climate, would set where mangroves can live in the northern Red Sea, and the sheltered lagoons of the north would be the first places to watch, and to protect, as the climate changes.
spec.ev: Duba (27.43 N, 35.60 E): the KSLOF Atlas gives Sharm Zubeir (27°25′N) as the northern limit of grey mangrove on the Saudi coast; Al-Hasawi (2022) sampled mangroves at a Duba station at the same latitude, described as an inland lagoon away from human activities and the northernmost of ten stations between Duba and Al-Birk; the same study cites about 135 km² of mangroves on the Saudi Red Sea coast. Al Wajh (25.6 N, 36.8 E): a 2,081 km² lagoon enclosed by a barrier reef, with 92 islands, coral reefs, seagrass beds and mangroves; the reef corals of the northern Red Sea are among the most heat-tolerant known. Qishran Bay (20.26 N, 40.04 E): a shallow bay of about 15 × 35 km almost enclosed by a long, narrow island and eight smaller islets, most fringed by Avicennia mangroves, with dense Salicornia and seagrass beds. In all three records the mangroves grow in enclosed or island-sheltered water; the records give no comparison with open shores.
spec.an: In Florida, Cavanaugh and colleagues (2014) used decades of satellite images to show that mangroves on the Atlantic coast spread northward as extreme winter cold became less frequent, showing that a mangrove limit can be set by the harshest conditions rather than by the average.
spec.val: Map every mangrove stand on the Saudi Red Sea coast from the KSLOF Atlas and recent satellite images; classify each by setting (enclosed sharm or lagoon, behind a barrier reef or island, or open shore); compare the share of sheltered stands north and south of about 25°N; log winter water temperature and salinity inside and just outside sheltered lagoons near Duba and Al Wajh for several years.
dlist: Rival explanation 1: the limit is set by the temperature and salinity of the open sea alone, and the shape of the coast makes no difference.
Rival explanation 2: sheltered places simply hold the soft mud that mangroves need to take root; sediment, not calm or warmth, explains the pattern.
Rival explanation 3: on open, easily reached shores, people and grazing animals removed mangroves, so the pattern records human access, not nature.
refs: Bruckner, A., Rowlands, G., Riegl, B., Purkis, S., Williams, A. & Renaud, P. (2012). Khaled bin Sultan Living Oceans Foundation Atlas of Saudi Arabian Red Sea Marine Habitats. Panoramic Press.
Al-Hasawi, Z.M. (2022). Determination of potentially toxic metals in mangrove trees and associated sediments along Saudi Red Sea coast. Egyptian Journal of Aquatic Biology & Fisheries 26(6), 595–617.

Chalastani, V. I., Manetos, P., Al-Suwailem, A. M. et al. (2020). Reconciling tourism development and conservation outcomes through marine spatial planning for a Saudi Giga-Project in the Red Sea. Frontiers in Marine Science 7, 168.
Key Biodiversity Areas Partnership. Qishran Bay (KBA 8277) factsheet.
Cavanaugh, K. C. et al. (2014). Poleward expansion of mangroves is a threshold response to decreased frequency of extreme cold events. PNAS 111(2), 723–727.
spec.se: The most northerly mangroves on the Saudi Red Sea coast grow in an inland lagoon near Duba, and others farther south shelter behind reefs and islands. Does the shape of the coast decide where they can survive? Nobody has tested this yet.
spec.sa: تنمو أشجار القرم الأبعد شمالًا على ساحل البحر الأحمر السعودي في بحيرة داخلية قرب ضباء، وتحتمي غيرها في الجنوب خلف الشعاب والجزر. فهل يقرّر شكل الساحل أين تستطيع البقاء؟ لم يختبر أحد ذلك بعد.

spot.en: Born from three records on this map. The northernmost mangroves on the Saudi Red Sea coast grow near Duba in an inland lagoon; at Al Wajh, mangroves share a lagoon enclosed by a barrier reef; and at Qishran Bay they fringe islets that almost close the bay off from the sea. Each time, the mangroves stood behind a wall of reef or land.
spot.ar: وُلدت الفكرة من ثلاثة سجلات على هذه الخريطة: فأشجار القرم الأبعد شمالًا على ساحل البحر الأحمر السعودي تنمو قرب ضباء في بحيرة داخلية؛ وفي الوجه تتقاسم أشجار القرم بحيرة يحيط بها حاجز مرجاني؛ وفي خليج قشران تحفّ جُزُرًا تكاد تعزل الخليج عن البحر. وفي كل مرة كانت أشجار القرم تقف خلف جدار من الشعاب أو اليابسة.

pred.en: North of about 25°N, nearly all mangrove stands will lie inside enclosed lagoons or sharms or behind reefs and islands, while farther south a clear share will grow on open shores; and in winter the water inside the northern lagoons will be calmer and warmer than the open sea just outside.
pred.ar: شمال خط العرض 25° تقريبًا ستقع كل تجمّعات القرم تقريبًا داخل بحيرات أو شروم مغلقة أو خلف الشعاب والجزر، بينما ستنمو نسبة واضحة منها جنوبًا على شواطئ مكشوفة؛ وسيكون الماء داخل البحيرات الشمالية في الشتاء أهدأ وأدفأ من البحر المفتوح خارجها مباشرة.

test.en: Map and classify every mangrove stand along the coast by its setting, compare the north with the south, and log winter temperature and salinity inside and outside the northern lagoons.
test.ar: رسم خريطة لكل تجمّع للقرم على طول الساحل وتصنيفه بحسب موقعه، ومقارنة الشمال بالجنوب، وتسجيل حرارة الماء وملوحته في الشتاء داخل البحيرات الشمالية وخارجها.

wrong.en: If northern mangroves grow on open shores as often as southern ones, or if the sheltered lagoons are no warmer or calmer in winter than the open sea, the idea fails.
wrong.ar: إذا نمت أشجار القرم الشمالية على الشواطئ المكشوفة بقدر ما تنمو عليها الجنوبية، أو لم تكن البحيرات المحمية أدفأ أو أهدأ في الشتاء من البحر المفتوح، تسقط الفكرة.

tag.en: At the northern edge of their range, mangroves may need the coast to shelter them
tag.ar: عند الحافة الشمالية لموطنها، ربما تحتاج أشجار القرم إلى ساحل يحميها

en: Mangroves are trees that live with their roots in the sea. Along the Saudi Red Sea coast there are about 135 square kilometres of them. But travel north and they thin out, until near Duba, at about 27°25′N, the last grey mangroves grow in an inland lagoon.

Look at the other stands on this map and something repeats. At Al Wajh the mangroves share a lagoon closed off by a barrier reef. At Qishran Bay they fringe little islets behind a long island. Again and again, there is a wall between them and the open sea.
ar: أشجار القرم أشجار تعيش وجذورها في البحر، وعلى ساحل البحر الأحمر السعودي منها نحو 135 كيلومترًا مربعًا. لكنها تقلّ كلما اتجهتَ شمالًا، حتى إذا بلغتَ ضباء، عند خط العرض 27°25′ تقريبًا، وجدت آخر أشجار القرم الرمادي تنمو في بحيرة داخلية.

وانظر إلى بقية مواقعها على هذه الخريطة تجد أمرًا يتكرر. ففي الوجه تتقاسم أشجار القرم بحيرة يغلقها حاجز مرجاني، وفي خليج قشران تحفّ جُزُرًا صغيرة خلف جزيرة طويلة. ومرة بعد مرة يقوم جدار بينها وبين البحر المفتوح.

h2.en: Seen before: the mangroves of Florida

en: Florida, in the United States, is another place where mangroves reach their northern edge. Cavanaugh and colleagues studied decades of satellite images of its Atlantic coast.

They found that the mangroves spread north as killing winter frosts became rarer. The limit was set not by the average winter but by the harshest nights. A small change in the worst conditions moved the whole edge.
ar: ولاية فلوريدا في الولايات المتحدة مكان آخر تبلغ فيه أشجار القرم حافتها الشمالية. وقد درس كافانو وزملاؤه صورًا فضائية لساحلها الأطلسي على مدى عقود.
فوجدوا أن أشجار القرم امتدت شمالًا كلما صار الصقيع الشتوي القاتل أندر. فلم يكن الحدَّ يرسمه الشتاء المعتاد، بل أقسى لياليه. وتغيّرٌ صغير في أسوأ الظروف حرّك الحافة كلها.

en: Put the two together. If the cooler, saltier north is too harsh for mangroves on open shores, the last trees should survive only where reefs, islands and lagoons calm the water. Then nearly every northern stand should sit behind a wall, while farther south more of them should face the open sea.

It could be otherwise. Sheltered places may simply hold the soft mud that young mangroves need, or people may have cleared the easy-to-reach shores. Mapping every stand, and measuring the water inside and outside the lagoons, can tell.
ar: اجمع الأمرين. إذا كان الشمال، ببرودته وملوحته، أقسى من أن تحتمله أشجار القرم على الشواطئ المكشوفة، فلن تبقى آخر الأشجار إلا حيث تهدّئ الشعاب والجزر والبحيرات الماء. وعندئذ ينبغي أن يقف كل تجمّع شمالي تقريبًا خلف جدار، وأن يواجه مزيد منها البحر المفتوح كلما اتجهنا جنوبًا.

وقد يكون الأمر غير ذلك. فربما تحوي الأماكن المحمية ببساطة الطين الليّن الذي تحتاج إليه بادرات القرم، أو ربما أزال الناس الأشجار من الشواطئ السهلة الوصول. ورسم خريطة لكل تجمّع، وقياس الماء داخل البحيرات وخارجها، يستطيعان أن يحسما الأمر.

spec.n: Stone Hives on a Staircase of Flowers
spec.na: خلايا حجرية على سلّم من الأزهار
spec.te: Was the great stone apiary of Kherfi built where the mountain offers flowers at every height?
spec.ta: هل بُني منحل الخرفي الحجري العظيم حيث يقدّم الجبل أزهارًا على كل ارتفاع؟
spec.desc: A connection between three records on this map. At the abandoned village of Kherfi in Maysan, south of Taif, a stone apiary probably about 500 years old could hold some 1,300 beehives on different levels, lining curved terraces cut into a steep mountainside and made for beekeeping as well as farming. To the north-west, the Taif escarpment climbs from about 500 m in Wadi Nu’man to some 2,600 m within a strip about 10 km wide; its higher slopes are moister, and along its lip two juniper species overlap. To the south-east, near Baljurashi, a survey of the same Sarawat mountains recorded 319 plant species, with Erica arborea above 2,000 m and the richest plots on high slopes. The idea: on the steep Sarawat, a short bee flight up or down the mountain crosses several belts of plants, and Kherfi’s builders crowded so many hives onto a steep slope because it could feed bees from many belts; old wax and debris in the hive chambers should therefore hold pollen from plants of many heights.
spec.sig: If true, the stone apiaries of the Sarawat would be a record of the mountain’s flowers as well as of its beekeeping, and protecting the plant-rich slopes around them would be part of protecting this heritage.
spec.ev: Kherfi (20.80 N, 40.76 E): apiaries probably about 500 years old, passed down within one family; room for about 1,300 hives on different levels; solid stone with stone columns supporting the upper floors; hives on curved terraces cut into a steep mountainside, made for beekeeping as well as farming; a 20 m stone fortress overlooks them (UNESCO Tentative List 2023, Rural Cultural Landscapes of Sarawat Mountains). Taif escarpment (21.19 N, 40.26 E; about 67 km from Kherfi): granitic, about 40 × 10 km, from about 500 m to some 2,600 m; higher slopes moister; the only place in Arabia where Juniperus phoenicia and J. excelsa overlap to any extent. Baljurashi (19.46 N, 41.37 E; about 160 km from Kherfi): 97 plots over 167.6 km² recorded 319 species in 228 genera and 75 families, 39 of them rare or endangered; Juniperus procera in 49% of plots; Erica arborea above 2,000 m; richest plots on high-altitude slopes. The records give no pollen or honey data for Kherfi itself.
spec.an: Pollen grains caught in honey and wax can be identified under the microscope; the method, melissopalynology, is used around the world to tell which plants bees visited and where a honey came from, and in mountain regions honeys gathered at different heights often carry different mixtures of pollen.
spec.val: Collect old wax, comb fragments and debris from the hive chambers at Kherfi and date them where possible; identify their pollen under the microscope; survey the flowering plants on the slopes around Kherfi month by month and by altitude; match the pollen to the plants of each belt; repeat for traditional apiaries on gentler ground to see whether steep sites give more kinds of pollen.
dlist: Rival explanation 1: the apiary stood where the family and its fortress already were; safety and ownership, not flowers, decided the place.
Rival explanation 2: the stone chambers were built mainly to shield the hives from heat, wind and thieves, and any slope near the village would have done.
Rival explanation 3: beekeepers moved their hives between heights with the seasons, so the bees fed wherever the hives were carried, not on the slope below Kherfi.

spec.se: South of Taif, one family’s stone apiary held room for some 1,300 beehives on a steep mountainside, in mountains whose plants change as the slopes climb. Did the bees climb a staircase of flowers? Nobody has tested this yet.
spec.sa: جنوب الطائف اتّسع منحل حجري لأسرة واحدة لنحو 1,300 خلية نحل على سفح جبلي شديد الانحدار، في جبال تتبدّل نباتاتها كلما ارتفعت سفوحها. فهل صعد النحل سلّمًا من الأزهار؟ لم يختبر أحد ذلك بعد.

spot.en: Born from three records on this map. Kherfi’s stone apiary, with room for about 1,300 hives, lines terraces on a steep mountainside; the Taif escarpment to the north-west climbs from about 500 m to some 2,600 m in a strip only 10 km wide, with moister slopes at the top; and near Baljurashi, 319 plant species were counted on the same mountains, the richest on high slopes. A great apiary and a steep ladder of plants kept appearing side by side.
spot.ar: وُلدت الفكرة من ثلاثة سجلات على هذه الخريطة: فمنحل الخرفي الحجري، الذي يتّسع لنحو 1,300 خلية، يصطفّ على مدرّجات في سفح جبلي شديد الانحدار؛ وجرف الطائف إلى الشمال الغربي منه يرتفع من نحو 500 متر إلى قرابة 2,600 متر في شريط لا يزيد عرضه على 10 كيلومترات، ومنحدراته العليا أكثر رطوبة؛ وقرب بلجرشي أُحصي 319 نوعًا نباتيًا في الجبال نفسها، أغناها على المنحدرات العالية. فقد ظل المنحل العظيم وسلّم النباتات الشاهق يظهران جنبًا إلى جنب.

pred.en: Pollen in old wax and debris from the Kherfi hive chambers will come from many plants of different altitude belts, including plants of the higher, moister slopes such as tree heath (Erica arborea), and from more kinds of plants than pollen from traditional apiaries on gentler ground.
pred.ar: ستأتي حبوب اللقاح في الشمع القديم والفتات المأخوذ من حجرات الخلايا في الخرفي من نباتات كثيرة تنتمي إلى نطاقات ارتفاع مختلفة، بينها نباتات المنحدرات العليا الأكثر رطوبة مثل الخلنج الشجري (Erica arborea)، ومن أنواع نباتية أكثر مما تحويه حبوب اللقاح في مناحل تقليدية على أراضٍ أقل انحدارًا.

test.en: Identify the pollen in old wax and debris from the hive chambers, survey the flowering plants around Kherfi by month and by height, and compare with apiaries on gentler slopes.

tag.en: An old stone apiary near Taif may have been built to reach the flowers of a whole mountain
tag.ar: ربما بُني منحل حجري قديم قرب الطائف ليبلغ نحله أزهار جبل بأكمله

en: South of Taif, at the abandoned village of Kherfi, a mountainside is lined with stone. Curved terraces climb the slope, and in their walls are chambers for beehives, stacked on different levels like the floors of a tall building, with stone columns holding up the upper rows.

There is room for about 1,300 hives. The apiary is probably some 500 years old and was handed down within one family, watched over by a stone fortress 20 metres high. Why build so many hives, so carefully, on such a steep slope?
ar: جنوب الطائف، في قرية الخرفي المهجورة، يكسو الحجر سفح جبل. تصعد المدرّجات المنحنية مع المنحدر، وفي جدرانها حجرات لخلايا النحل مصفوفة على مستويات مختلفة كطوابق مبنى شاهق، تحمل أعمدة حجرية صفوفها العليا.

يتّسع المكان لنحو 1,300 خلية. ويُرجَّح أن عمر المنحل نحو 500 عام، وأنه انتقل من جيل إلى جيل داخل أسرة واحدة، يحرسه حصن حجري ارتفاعه 20 مترًا. فلماذا تُبنى كل هذه الخلايا، بكل هذه العناية، على منحدر بهذه الحدّة؟

h2.en: Seen before: honey that remembers its flowers
h2.ar: حدث من قبل: عسل يتذكّر أزهاره

en: Every time a bee visits a flower, it carries away tiny grains of pollen, and some of them end up in the honey and the wax. Under a microscope, each plant’s pollen has a shape of its own.

Scientists around the world use this method, called melissopalynology, to tell which flowers bees visited and where a honey came from. In mountain lands, honeys gathered at different heights often carry different mixtures of pollen.
ar: كلما زارت نحلة زهرة حملت منها حبيبات دقيقة من اللقاح، ينتهي بعضها في العسل والشمع. وتحت المجهر يكون لحبوب لقاح كل نبات شكلها الخاص.

ويستعمل العلماء حول العالم هذه الطريقة، التي تُسمّى تحليل حبوب اللقاح في العسل، ليعرفوا الأزهار التي زارها النحل والمكان الذي جاء منه العسل. وفي البلاد الجبلية كثيرًا ما يحمل العسل المجموع على ارتفاعات مختلفة مزيجًا مختلفًا من حبوب اللقاح.

en: Now look at the mountains around Kherfi. The Taif escarpment climbs from about 500 metres to some 2,600 metres, and its higher slopes are moister. Near Baljurashi, botanists counted 319 kinds of plants, the richest on the high slopes. If Kherfi’s bees could reach many plant belts in a short flight, the old wax in its stone chambers should hold pollen from many of them.
But perhaps the hives simply stood where the family and its fortress already were, safe from heat and thieves. The pollen hidden in the old chambers could tell which story is true.
ar: انظر الآن إلى الجبال حول الخرفي. يرتفع جرف الطائف من نحو 500 متر إلى قرابة 2,600 متر، ومنحدراته العليا أكثر رطوبة. وقرب بلجرشي أحصى علماء النبات 319 نوعًا من النباتات، أغناها على المنحدرات العالية. فإن كان نحل الخرفي يبلغ نطاقات نباتية كثيرة في طيران قصير، فينبغي أن يحمل الشمع القديم في حجراته الحجرية حبوب لقاح من كثير منها.
ولكن ربما وُضعت الخلايا ببساطة حيث كانت الأسرة وحصنها، في مأمن من الحر واللصوص. وحبوب اللقاح المختبئة في الحجرات القديمة تستطيع أن تخبرنا أيّ الحكايتين هي الصحيحة.
